learningObjectives: Choose between Microsoft Entra registered, Microsoft Entra joined and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined for a given device and ownership model

Select the correct enrollment method for iOS/iPadOS, macOS and Android (BYOD vs corporate)

modules.executiveSummary:
Every Intune scenario starts with two questions: **what identity does the device have in Microsoft Entra ID** and **how does it get enrolled into Intune**. A device identity (registered, joined or hybrid joined) is the prerequisite for device-based Conditional Access and MDM. Enrollment then depends on platform and ownership: Windows uses automatic enrollment (often via Autopilot), Apple corporate devices use Automated Device Enrollment from Apple Business Manager, Android corporate devices use Android Enterprise profiles (fully managed, dedicated or corporate-owned work profile), and personal devices use user-initiated enrollment or no enrollment at all (MAM only).

For MD-102 you must be able to read a scenario (who owns the device, what platform, does it need on-premises AD) and pick the identity, the group strategy and the enrollment method in one go.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A device identity for personal (BYOD) devices and mobile phones; the user signs in with a work account but the device is not joined to the directory.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Gives SSO and allows the device to be evaluated by Conditional Access without the organisation taking ownership of the device.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Organisation-owned Windows 10/11 devices joined directly to Microsoft Entra ID with no on-premises AD join.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: The cloud-native target state for corporate Windows devices; supports Autopilot, Windows Hello for Business and SSO to on-premises resources.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Devices joined to on-premises AD and registered in Microsoft Entra ID; needs line of sight to domain controllers.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: An interim step for organisations with legacy AD dependencies. Microsoft no longer recommends it for new devices, including via Autopilot.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: The automatic enrollment setting (None/Some/All) that decides which users' Windows devices auto-enroll into Intune when joined or registered.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Without it, Entra join and Autopilot do not result in Intune management.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Apple's zero-touch corporate enrollment; Intune trusts Apple Business Manager through an enrollment program token (.p7m) that must be renewed yearly.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Makes devices supervised and enrolled from the Setup Assistant, which unlocks stronger management and prevents removal of management.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Fully managed (COBO), dedicated (COSU/kiosk) and corporate-owned with work profile (COPE); personal devices use personally owned work profile.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Each mode balances control and privacy differently; Android device administrator is deprecated on GMS devices.

modules.deepDive:
### Choosing the device identity

| Scenario | Identity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Personal Windows laptop, phone, tablet | Microsoft Entra registered | User adds work account; can still be MDM-enrolled if MDM user scope applies |
| New corporate Windows 11 laptop | Microsoft Entra joined | Default for Autopilot; cloud-native |
| Existing domain-joined PC with GPO dependencies | Microsoft Entra hybrid joined | Requires Entra Connect; not recommended for new devices |

Device identities are a prerequisite for device-based Conditional Access and for Intune MDM. A device must be registered in Entra ID before it can be marked compliant.

### Groups

- **Assigned groups**: manual membership, ideal for pilots and labs.
- **Dynamic device groups**: rule-based. The classic Autopilot rule is (device.devicePhysicalIDs -any (_ -startsWith "[ZTDid]")). Group tags map to the OrderID attribute: (device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[OrderID]:KANTOOR-GENT")).
- Dynamic membership evaluation is not instant; Autopilot device preparation solves this with **enrollment time grouping** (the device is added to a static group at enrollment).

### Windows enrollment

- **Automatic enrollment** in Intune admin center > Devices > Enrollment > Windows > Automatic Enrollment: set MDM user scope to All or Some. Requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 (included in M365 Business Premium and E3).
- Users must be allowed to join devices to Entra ID (Entra > Devices > Device settings).
- **Enrollment restrictions** (platform and device limit) can block personally owned Windows enrollment; corporate identifiers or Autopilot registration mark devices as corporate so they are not blocked.
- Other methods: bulk enrollment with a provisioning package (Windows Configuration Designer), GPO-based auto-enrollment for hybrid joined devices, co-management.

### Apple

- **BYOD iOS/iPadOS**: user enrollment or device enrollment through Company Portal; macOS BYOD through Company Portal.
- **Corporate**: ADE via Apple Business Manager. Steps: download Intune public key > create MDM server in ABM and download the token (.p7m) > upload token with the managed Apple ID > create an enrollment profile (user affinity, Setup Assistant panes) > sync and assign devices.
- An **Apple MDM push certificate** is required for any Apple management and must be renewed annually with the same Apple ID.

### Android

- Connect Intune to **Managed Google Play** first (required for every Android Enterprise mode).
- Corporate provisioning: QR code (recommended), token entry via afw#setup, NFC, **Google zero-touch** (reseller devices) or **Samsung Knox Mobile Enrollment**.
- BYOD: personally owned work profile through Company Portal.
modules.architecture:
1. **Identity layer** - Microsoft Entra ID holds the device object (deviceId, trustType, physical IDs such as ZTDId/OrderID). The device receives a Primary Refresh Token, used for SSO and for Conditional Access device claims.
2. **Enrollment layer** - the MDM discovery URL and terms-of-use URL configured under Mobility (MDM and WIP) point Windows to Intune. For Apple, the APNs certificate and ADE token establish trust between Apple's services and Intune. For Android, the Managed Google Play binding lets Intune create enrollment profiles and tokens.
3. **Grouping layer** - Entra groups (assigned or dynamic) are the targeting unit for every Intune policy, app and profile; filters refine at assignment time.
4. **Management channel** - after enrollment the device checks in to Intune (Windows via OMA-DM/CSPs plus the Intune Management Extension for Win32 apps and scripts; Apple via MDM/DDM; Android via Android Device Policy).

Ownership (corporate vs personal) is stored on the Intune device object and drives which actions are possible (for example full wipe is limited on personal devices and inventory is reduced).
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: 40-user accountancy firm in Ghent, managed by our MSP**

The firm has 35 Windows laptops (5 years old, domain-joined to a single DC in the office), 40 company iPhones and a handful of personal Android phones used for Teams and Outlook.

Our approach:

- New laptops are bought through a partner that registers hardware hashes in Autopilot; they become **Microsoft Entra joined** and auto-enroll (MDM user scope = All, licensed via Microsoft 365 Business Premium). Old domain-joined laptops are left hybrid joined until their refresh, not migrated in place.
- A dynamic device group uses the group tag **ACC-GENT** so policies target only this customer's devices in our multi-customer runbook.
- iPhones are bought via an Apple reseller linked to the firm's **Apple Business Manager**; an ADE token is uploaded in Intune and phones are supervised. We document the managed Apple ID and the APNs renewal date in the customer's documentation and in our PSA as a recurring task.
- Personal Android phones are **not enrolled**: they get app protection policies only (see the MAM module), keeping the partners happy about privacy.

Result: zero-touch onboarding for new staff and a clear split between company and personal devices that the auditor of the firm can follow.
examTips: If a scenario says 'personal device' and 'no device management', think Microsoft Entra registered plus app protection, not enrollment.
Hybrid join needs on-premises AD connectivity; Microsoft recommends Entra join for all new devices, including Autopilot deployments.
ADE requires Apple Business Manager (or Apple School Manager) plus an enrollment program token; the APNs certificate is a separate prerequisite.
Android Enterprise requires binding to Managed Google Play first; Android device administrator is deprecated on GMS devices.
Automatic Windows enrollment is configured by the MDM user scope and requires Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2.
Group tag in Autopilot maps to the OrderID attribute in Entra dynamic rules; ZTDId identifies any Autopilot-registered device.
commonPitfalls: Letting the APNs certificate or ADE token expire; renewing APNs with a different Apple ID forces re-enrollment of every Apple device.
Blocking personal Windows enrollment without registering devices in Autopilot or adding corporate identifiers, which blocks legitimate corporate devices.
Using a dynamic group based on attributes that only exist after enrollment to target Autopilot profiles, so devices are not in the group during OOBE.
Setting both MDM user scope and MAM (WIP) user scope for the same users without understanding which wins on corporate vs personal devices.
fieldExperience: Keep a shared, MFA-protected managed Apple ID per customer for APNs and ADE; personal Apple IDs of a former employee are the number one cause of painful Apple re-enrollments.
For SMB tenants we standardise group naming (CUST-DEV-Autopilot, CUST-USR-Pilot) so filters and assignments look identical across customers and runbooks can be reused.
Samsung Knox Mobile Enrollment is worth it as soon as a customer buys more than a handful of Samsung devices; it avoids the afw#setup typing session on every phone.
revisionNotes: Registered = BYOD; Joined = corporate cloud-native; Hybrid = corporate with on-prem AD (legacy).
Autopilot dynamic rule: devicePhysicalIDs -any _ -startsWith "[ZTDid]"; group tag = [OrderID].
Apple: APNs certificate (all Apple MDM) + ADE token (corporate, from ABM, renewed yearly).
Android corporate: QR / token (afw#setup) / NFC / zero-touch / Knox; BYOD = personally owned work profile.
Enrollment restrictions: platform and device limit; corporate identifiers bypass personal-device blocks.

modules.title: RBAC, compliance, Conditional Access, Windows Hello for Business and Windows LAPS
learningObjectives: Assign built-in and custom Intune roles with scope groups and scope tags, and protect sensitive changes with Multi Admin Approval
Design compliance policies per platform, including actions for noncompliance and tenant-wide compliance settings
Build a Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device and roll it out safely

Deploy Windows LAPS with Intune and Microsoft Entra ID and manage local group membership
modules.executiveSummary:
This module covers the 'who may do what' and 'which device may access what' parts of the exam. **Intune RBAC** controls admins: a role (permissions) + members (admin group) + scope (groups) + scope tags (visibility). **Compliance policies** evaluate device state and report it to Microsoft Entra ID; **Conditional Access** decides access based on that state. Remember the split: compliance evaluates, Conditional Access enforces.

On top of that, Windows-specific identity hardening is tested: **Windows Hello for Business** (tenant-wide enrollment policy vs account protection policy), **Windows LAPS** through the endpoint security account protection node with backup to Microsoft Entra ID, and the **Local user group membership** profile to lock down the local Administrators group.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A role assignment links a role to admin group members and to scope groups; scope tags limit which objects (policies, apps, devices) admins can see.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Supports least privilege and distributed IT, such as an MSP helpdesk that may only see one site's devices.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Access policies that require a second admin to approve changes to protected resources such as apps, scripts or RBAC.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Prevents a single compromised or careless admin account from pushing destructive changes.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Per-platform rules (OS version, encryption, password, Defender risk score, jailbreak) plus actions for noncompliance (mark noncompliant after N days, notify, retire).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Produces a trustworthy compliance state that Conditional Access can consume.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' (default Compliant) and 'Compliance status validity period' (default 30 days, 1-120).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Closes gaps for devices without a policy or that stop checking in.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Built-in Windows feature that manages one local admin account per device, rotates its password and backs it up to Microsoft Entra ID or AD.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Removes shared local admin passwords and mitigates pass-the-hash and lateral movement.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Device-bound, PIN/biometric-based credential that replaces passwords; configurable tenant-wide at enrollment or per group afterwards.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Phishing-resistant sign-in that also satisfies MFA requirements in Conditional Access.

modules.deepDive:
### Intune RBAC

- Built-in roles include Policy and Profile Manager, Application Manager, Endpoint Security Manager, Help Desk Operator, Read Only Operator and Intune Role Administrator. Creating/assigning roles requires the Microsoft Entra **Intune Administrator** (Intune Service Administrator) role.
- A role assignment = **Members** (admin groups) + **Scope (Groups)** (users/devices they manage) + **Scope tags**.
- Permissions from multiple assignments are cumulative; there is no deny. By default permissions can merge across assignments with different scope tags; an opt-in 'scoped permissions' preview contains them per assignment.
- Windows 365 has its own built-in roles (for example Cloud PC Administrator) managed alongside Intune roles.
- **Multi Admin Approval** access policies protect apps, scripts, compliance scripts and role changes; the approver must be a different admin.

### Compliance and Conditional Access

1. Create compliance policies per platform (Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android Enterprise, macOS, Linux). Typical Windows settings: BitLocker, Secure Boot, minimum OS version, firewall, Defender antimalware, device risk score from Defender for Endpoint.
2. Configure **actions for noncompliance**: mark noncompliant immediately or after a grace period, email/push notification, remote lock, retire.
3. Change tenant-wide **Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as** to **Not compliant** when using Conditional Access.
4. In Entra admin center > Conditional Access, create a policy: users (exclude break-glass accounts), target resources, grant **Require device to be marked as compliant**. Start in **Report-only**, then switch On.

Key behaviours:
- Compliance policies take precedence over configuration policies for the same setting; multiple compliance policies resolve to the most restrictive value.
- A setting in **Error** keeps the existing compliance state for up to 7 days.
- 'Require device to be marked as compliant' does **not** block Intune enrollment itself.
- Custom compliance (PowerShell discovery script + JSON rules) extends Windows and Linux compliance.

### Windows Hello for Business

- **Tenant-wide policy**: Devices > Windows > Enrollment > Windows Hello for Business; applies to all devices at enrollment only.
- After enrollment: endpoint security **Account protection** profile, settings catalog or security baselines.
- Entra joined devices enable WHfB by default unless disabled.

### Windows LAPS

1. Enable LAPS in Microsoft Entra ID (Devices > Device settings > Enable Microsoft Entra Local Administrator Password Solution).
2. Intune > Endpoint security > Account protection > Create policy > Windows > **Local admin password solution (Windows LAPS)**.
3. Set **Backup Directory** (Microsoft Entra ID for Entra joined devices; AD for hybrid if desired), password complexity/length, PasswordAgeDays, post-authentication actions.
4. Assign to **device groups** (not user groups) and use a single LAPS policy per device.
5. View the password on the device's Local admin password blade; use the **Rotate local admin password** device action (requires Remote tasks: Rotate Local Admin Password permission).

LAPS does not create accounts; it manages an existing account (built-in Administrator by RID if Administrator Account Name is blank). Use **Local user group membership** (account protection) or a settings catalog policy to control who sits in local Administrators.
modules.architecture:
**Compliance flow**: Intune evaluates device settings on check-in > writes complianceState to the Intune device > Intune reports isCompliant to the Entra device object > during sign-in, Conditional Access reads the device claim from the PRT/device certificate and evaluates grant controls.

**RBAC flow**: Intune role definition (permissions) + role assignment (members, scope groups, scope tags). Every Intune object carries scope tags; the admin center filters lists by the intersection of the admin's tags.

**LAPS flow**: Intune delivers the LAPS CSP configuration > the Windows LAPS client on the device rotates the password per policy > the encrypted password is stored on the Entra device object (deviceLocalCredentials) > authorised admins read it from Entra or Intune; all reads and manual rotations are audited.

**WHfB**: on Entra joined devices the user provisions a TPM-bound key during first sign-in (after MFA). The public key is registered in Entra ID; authentication uses the private key unlocked by PIN/biometric.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: securing the accountancy firm before a cyber-insurance audit**

- **RBAC**: our first-line helpdesk gets a custom role (read devices, sync, restart, rotate LAPS password, offer Remote Help) scoped with the tag ACC-GENT. Only senior engineers hold Policy and Profile Manager. Multi Admin Approval protects app and script deployments because one bad PowerShell script can hit all 35 laptops at once.
- **Compliance**: Windows policy requires BitLocker, Secure Boot, Defender up to date and Windows 11 minimum build; iOS policy requires a passcode and a supported iOS version. Grace period of 3 days with an email notification in Dutch.
- **Conditional Access**: 'Require compliant device' for all cloud apps on Windows and macOS, report-only for one week, break-glass accounts excluded. Tenant setting changed to treat devices without compliance policy as Not compliant.
- **LAPS**: one policy, backup to Microsoft Entra ID, 14 characters complex, rotation every 30 days and 'reset password and log off' after use. Users are standard users (Autopilot profile) and local Administrators membership is enforced with the Local user group membership profile.

The insurer's questionnaire items (MFA, no shared admin passwords, encrypted endpoints) can now be answered with Intune reports as evidence.
examTips: Compliance policies evaluate; Conditional Access enforces. A question asking to 'block access' always needs a CA policy too.
Set 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' to Not compliant when compliance is used with Conditional Access.
Compliance status validity period default is 30 days (range 1-120); a device that doesn't report in that window becomes noncompliant.
Windows LAPS policies live under Endpoint security > Account protection; assign to device groups and enable LAPS in Entra device settings first.
The tenant-wide WHfB policy applies only at enrollment time; use account protection or settings catalog for targeted changes afterwards.
Scope tags control visibility, roles control actions. Creating and assigning Intune roles needs the Intune Administrator Entra role.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting to exclude break-glass accounts from a 'require compliant device' policy for all users and all resources.
Assigning LAPS to user groups or multiple overlapping LAPS policies, causing conflicts and failed backups.
Choosing Active Directory as LAPS backup directory for cloud-only Entra joined devices: the policy applies but backup silently fails.
Expecting a configuration profile to fix compliance: if the same setting is in a compliance policy, the compliance value wins.
fieldExperience: Always run new Conditional Access policies in Report-only for at least a week and check the sign-in logs' report-only tab; SMB customers have more unmanaged edge cases (scanners, shared mailboxes, accountant's home PC) than they think.
Combine LAPS with the 'Local user group membership' profile; otherwise a user who was made local admin years ago remains admin and LAPS gives a false sense of control.
Document the compliance grace period in the customer's SLA so the service desk knows why a laptop is 'In grace period' and not blocked yet.
revisionNotes: Role assignment = members + scope groups + scope tags; permissions are additive, no deny.
CA grant 'Require device to be marked as compliant' supports Windows, iOS, Android, macOS and Linux Ubuntu enrolled in Intune.
Error state in a compliance setting keeps the previous state for up to 7 days.
LAPS: Entra toggle + account protection LAPS profile + device groups; manual rotation = device action.
WHfB: tenant-wide at enrollment vs account protection/settings catalog post-enrollment.

modules.executiveSummary:
Windows Autopilot turns an OEM-installed Windows image into a business-ready device without imaging. Two flavours exist: classic **Autopilot deployment profiles** (requires hardware hash registration, supports user-driven, pre-provisioning and self-deploying, hybrid join) and **Autopilot device preparation** (no hash registration needed, uses enrollment time grouping and a device group, granular reporting, user-driven Entra join and an automatic mode for Windows 365). The **Enrollment Status Page** blocks the desktop until required apps and policies are installed.

The same domain covers Windows 11 upgrades through feature update policies, Windows 365 Cloud PC provisioning (provisioning policy, Microsoft-hosted network vs Azure network connection, gallery vs custom image) and Windows Backup for Organizations, which restores user settings during OOBE.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A device fingerprint uploaded by the OEM/reseller or manually (CSV or Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo) to register a device for classic Autopilot.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Lets the Autopilot service recognise the device at OOBE and deliver the assigned deployment profile.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: The user signs in during OOBE; the device joins Entra ID (or hybrid) and enrolls in Intune, associated with that user.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: The standard 1:1 knowledge-worker scenario; works on virtual machines, so it is ideal for labs.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A technician (or reseller) runs the device phase in advance by pressing the Windows key five times, then reseals; the user only completes the user phase.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Reduces the time the end user waits; needs physical TPM 2.0 with attestation and an ESP.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: No user credentials; the device authenticates with TPM 2.0 attestation and joins Entra ID automatically.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Kiosks, shared devices and meeting room PCs. Not supported on VMs (0x800705B4 timeout).

coreConcepts.whatItIs: OOBE/first-sign-in progress page that can block device use until all or selected apps and profiles are installed.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Ensures security baselines and line-of-business apps are present before the user starts working.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Newer policy type: device group + up to 25 apps and 10 scripts installed during OOBE, enrollment time grouping and near real-time reporting.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Simpler, faster and more observable deployments without hash pre-registration; also used for Windows 365 automatic mode.

modules.deepDive:
### Profile vs device preparation

| Capability | Deployment profile | Device preparation |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware hash registration | Required | Not required (corporate identifiers or device association optional) |
| Modes | User-driven, pre-provisioning, self-deploying | User-driven, automatic (Windows 365) |
| Hybrid join | Supported (not recommended) | Entra join |
| Device targeting | Dynamic/assigned group of registered devices | Enrollment time grouping into a static device group |
| App delivery during OOBE | ESP tracks assigned apps | Up to 25 selected apps + 10 scripts in the policy |
| Reporting | ESP + Autopilot deployments report | Granular near real-time deployment report |

### Classic Autopilot flow (user-driven Entra join)

1. Set MDM user scope; allow users to join devices to Entra ID.
2. Register devices (OEM/CSP partner or manual hash import).
3. Create a device group (dynamic ZTDId or group tag rule).
4. Create and assign an ESP profile.
5. Create an Autopilot deployment profile: Deployment mode = User-driven, Join to Microsoft Entra ID as = Microsoft Entra joined, hide EULA/privacy/change account options, user account type Standard, optional **Apply device name template** (max 15 characters, letters/numbers/hyphens, macros %SERIAL% or %RAND:x%), optional Allow pre-provisioned deployment.
6. Optionally assign the device to a user; deploy.

'Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot' registers existing corporate devices in the targeted groups (allow up to 48 hours).

### ESP essentials

- Profiles are prioritised; device-targeted profiles win over user-targeted; default profile applies otherwise. Pre-provisioning and self-deploying only apply device-targeted profiles.
- **Block device use until all apps and profiles are installed** + **Block device use until these required apps are installed** (All or Selected).
- Apps must be **required** assignments; device-context apps are tracked in the device phase.
- Mixing LOB MSI and Win32 apps during ESP can cause install conflicts; prefer Win32 only. Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps as a Win32 package if it must be tracked during ESP.
- 'Install Windows quality updates' installs the monthly security update at the end of OOBE (adds 20-40 minutes).

### Windows 11 upgrade

- Create a **feature update policy** targeting a Windows 11 version; non-capable devices stay on Windows 10 unless you tick 'install the latest Windows 10 feature update' on incapable devices.
- Use Endpoint analytics **Work from anywhere** report to check Windows 11 hardware readiness.
- Feature update policies don't apply during OOBE; they apply at the first Windows Update scan after provisioning.

### Windows 365

- Provisioning policy (Devices > Provision Cloud PCs > Provisioning policies): experience type, license type (Enterprise, Frontline/Flex, Reserve), join type, network (**Microsoft-hosted network** recommended, or **Azure network connection** for hybrid join or direct on-premises connectivity), image (gallery or custom), optional Autopilot device preparation, user group assignment.
- Changes to a provisioning policy affect only newly provisioned or reprovisioned Cloud PCs.

### Windows Backup for Organizations

- Backup: settings catalog > Sync your settings > Enable Windows backup.
- Restore: Devices > Enrollment > Windows > Windows Backup and Restore > Show restore page = On (tenant-wide, Intune Service Administrator). Restore requires Entra joined devices and, with Autopilot, user-driven mode.
modules.architecture:
At first boot the device connects to the network and contacts the Autopilot deployment service (ztd.dds.microsoft.com) with its hardware hash. If registered, it downloads the assigned profile (JSON) that customises OOBE. The user authenticates against Entra ID, the device joins Entra ID and, because of the MDM user scope, auto-enrolls into Intune. Intune then delivers policies via CSPs; the Intune Management Extension installs Win32 apps and scripts; the ESP tracks progress through **Device preparation**, **Device setup** and **Account setup** phases.

Pre-provisioning and self-deploying use TPM 2.0 attestation (\*.microsoftaik.azure.net and firmware TPM vendor URLs) to prove device identity without user credentials. Device preparation instead uses enrollment time grouping: at enrollment Intune immediately adds the device to the policy's static device group so apps and scripts assigned to that group install during OOBE without waiting for dynamic group evaluation.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: laptop refresh for the accountancy firm**

- 12 new laptops are ordered from a Belgian reseller who uploads hashes with group tag ACC-GENT.
- Our MSP technician uses **pre-provisioning** in our workshop: apps (Microsoft 365 Apps as Win32, accounting software, PDF tool, VPN client) install during the technician flow, the device is resealed and shipped. On the first day the user just signs in, sets up Windows Hello and is working within 15 minutes.
- Device name template **ACC-%SERIAL%** is too long for many serials (15-character limit), so we use **ACC-%RAND:8%** and keep serial numbers in our CMDB.
- ESP blocks the desktop until Defender, BitLocker, the VPN and the accounting app are installed; the user can reset the device if installation fails.
- One partner works remotely from the Ardennes and gets a **Windows 365 Enterprise** Cloud PC on the Microsoft-hosted network with Autopilot device preparation, because the accounting app requires a fixed environment.
- Windows Backup for Organizations is enabled so that replacing a broken laptop restores the user's settings during OOBE.
examTips: Self-deploying and pre-provisioning require physical TPM 2.0 with attestation; VMs (including Hyper-V vTPM) fail. User-driven works in VMs.
Device name template: max 15 characters, letters, numbers and hyphens, not all numbers; %SERIAL% and %RAND:x% macros.
Hybrid join through Autopilot needs the Intune Connector for Active Directory and a domain join profile; Microsoft no longer recommends it.
Autopilot device preparation does not need hardware hashes and uses enrollment time grouping; it can install up to 25 apps and 10 scripts during OOBE.
Windows 365: Microsoft-hosted network is the recommended default; Azure network connection is required for hybrid join or direct on-premises network access.
Feature update policies never downgrade and stay in effect until changed, unlike an update ring pause that expires after 35 days.
commonPitfalls: Assigning the Autopilot profile to a dynamic group based on attributes that do not exist before enrollment, so the device gets no profile at OOBE.
Mixing LOB (MSI) and Win32 apps in the ESP, causing TrustedInstaller conflicts and ESP timeouts.
Reusing a self-deployed or pre-provisioned device without deleting the Intune device record (error 0x80180014).
Forgetting to exclude the Microsoft Intune enrollment flow or using a device-based CA policy that blocks the Autopilot sign-in for new devices.
fieldExperience: For SMB customers user-driven Entra join with a solid ESP covers 90% of cases; pre-provisioning is worth it when we ship devices to remote users and want a 'just sign in' experience.
Always test the ESP on a Hyper-V VM with a checkpoint before the real devices arrive; it saves a day of reset loops when an app's detection rule is wrong.
Keep the Autopilot profile's user account type on Standard. Combined with EPM or LAPS that is the biggest security improvement an SMB gets from the refresh project.
revisionNotes: Modes: user-driven (user creds, VM ok), pre-provisioning (Win key x5, TPM 2.0), self-deploying (no user, TPM 2.0, kiosk).
ESP: device profile > user profile > default; block until all or selected required apps.
Device preparation: no hash, enrollment time grouping, 25 apps/10 scripts, W365 automatic mode.
Win11 upgrade = feature update policy; readiness = Endpoint analytics Work from anywhere report.
Windows 365: provisioning policy = network + image + configuration + user group assignment.

learningObjectives: Create configuration profiles with the settings catalog, templates, imported ADMX and custom OMA-URI

Configure profiles for iOS/iPadOS, macOS, Android and specialty devices
Target assignments with filters and understand include/exclude behaviour
Perform single and bulk remote actions, run device queries and collect diagnostics
modules.executiveSummary:
Configuration profiles are how Intune replaces Group Policy. The **settings catalog** is the preferred profile type for Windows, iOS/iPadOS and macOS; templates remain for certificates, VPN, Wi-Fi, email and a few others. **Group Policy analytics** imports GPO backups, shows MDM support per setting and can migrate supported settings straight into a settings catalog policy. **Assignment filters** refine group assignments at check-in using device properties such as model, OS version, ownership or enrollment profile name.

The second half covers operations: remote actions (sync, restart, retire, wipe, fresh start, Autopilot reset, rotate BitLocker keys, rotate local admin password, Defender quick scan and intelligence update), bulk device actions, **device query** with KQL and **diagnostics collection**.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A searchable list of thousands of settings generated directly from Windows CSPs and Apple payloads/DDM declarations.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: One consistent, future-proof profile type instead of dozens of fixed templates.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Imports GPO XML backups, reports MDM support percentage per setting and migrates supported settings to a settings catalog policy.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Speeds up the move from on-premises GPO to cloud-native management.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A rule (for example device.manufacturer -eq "Microsoft Corporation") applied in Include or Exclude mode on top of a group assignment.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Avoids creating many groups; evaluated quickly at check-in rather than relying on group membership calculation.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Retire removes company data, apps and policies but keeps personal data; Wipe resets the device to factory settings (optionally keeping enrollment state/user data on Windows).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Supports BYOD offboarding (retire) versus lost/stolen or reassigned corporate devices (wipe).

coreConcepts.whatItIs: On-demand KQL query against a single device (or many devices) for live data such as processes, services, registry, certificates.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Faster L1/L2 troubleshooting without a remote session; requires the Advanced Analytics licence.

modules.deepDive:
### Windows profiles

- **Settings catalog**: search, add, configure; reports per setting. Conflicts between profiles show as **Conflict** and the setting does not apply.
- **Administrative templates / ADMX import**: built-in ADMX-backed settings, and you can import third-party ADMX/ADML files (Devices > Configuration > Import ADMX) and configure them.
- **Custom (OMA-URI)** for CSP nodes not exposed elsewhere.
- **Group Policy analytics** (Devices > Manage devices > Group Policy analytics): import GPO backup XML, review 'MDM support', 'CSP mapping', then **Migrate** selected settings into a settings catalog profile. Conflicting values across GPOs are flagged during migration.

### Other platforms

- **iOS/iPadOS & macOS**: settings catalog (including DDM declarations), device features/restrictions templates (being migrated), Wi-Fi/VPN/email/certificate templates. Many restrictions require **supervised** devices (ADE).
- **Android Enterprise**: device restrictions for fully managed/dedicated/work profile, OEMConfig for Zebra/Samsung, kiosk (dedicated) settings.
- **Specialty**: Teams Rooms on Windows (settings catalog + LAPS), HoloLens 2 (Windows Holographic for Business; Autopilot for HoloLens), Zebra via OEMConfig and FOTA/LifeGuard for updates.

### Assignment filters

- Create in Tenant administration > Filters (managed devices or managed apps).
- Supported on apps, compliance policies, configuration profiles and app protection/app configuration (managed apps filters).
- Include = only matching devices within the group get it; Exclude = matching devices are skipped.
- Common properties: deviceName, manufacturer, model, osVersion, deviceOwnership, enrollmentProfileName, operatingSystemSKU.
- **Enrollment time grouping** (device preparation, and increasingly other flows) adds devices to a static group at enrollment to avoid dynamic group latency.

### Remote actions

| Action | Use |
|---|---|
| Sync | Force check-in |
| Restart | Reboot remotely |
| Retire | Remove org data (BYOD offboarding) |
| Wipe | Factory reset (options: retain enrollment state and user account; wipe even if power lost) |
| Fresh Start | Reinstall Windows, remove OEM apps |
| Autopilot Reset | Return Entra joined device to business-ready state keeping enrollment |
| BitLocker key rotation | Rotate recovery password after it was disclosed |
| Rotate local admin password | Immediate LAPS rotation |
| Update Windows Defender security intelligence / Quick scan / Full scan | Defender actions |
| Collect diagnostics | Upload logs (registry, event logs, IME logs) for Windows |

**Bulk device actions** (Devices > All devices > Bulk device actions) cover restart, rename, retire, wipe, sync, Autopilot reset and more for up to 100 devices per run.

The **Troubleshooting + support** blade shows per-user assignments, enrollment failures, app install failures and lets you collect diagnostics.
modules.architecture:
Windows MDM uses OMA-DM over HTTPS: on check-in (roughly every 8 hours, faster after enrollment, or on Sync), the device receives SyncML commands that set CSP nodes. Settings catalog policies are compiled into CSP operations; ADMX-backed settings are delivered through the Policy CSP ADMX ingestion. The Intune Management Extension (IME) handles Win32 apps, PowerShell scripts, Remediations and custom compliance.

Filters are evaluated by the Intune service at check-in against device properties reported by the device, so a filter change takes effect at the next check-in without group recalculation. Remote actions are queued commands sent via WNS/APNs/FCM push notification so the device checks in promptly.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: retiring the old domain GPOs**

The accountancy firm's 2016-era domain has 14 GPOs. We export them, import into **Group Policy analytics** and find 82% MDM-supported. Drive mappings and logon scripts are replaced by OneDrive/SharePoint shortcuts; legacy IE settings are dropped. The remaining settings are migrated to two settings catalog policies: 'ACC-WIN-Security' and 'ACC-WIN-UserExperience'.

The firm also has two Surface Hubs and one Teams Rooms device: a **filter** on model excludes them from the standard user-experience policy. A partner's stolen laptop is handled with **Wipe** (not retire), after we copy the BitLocker recovery key reference into the incident ticket; an employee leaving with a personal iPad gets **Retire** so only company data disappears.
examTips: Prefer the settings catalog for new Windows and Apple policies; templates remain for certificates, Wi-Fi, VPN, email and wired network.
Group Policy analytics needs the GPO exported as XML; only MDM-supported settings can be migrated to a settings catalog policy.
Filters refine an assignment; they don't replace groups. Exclude groups and filters are evaluated per assignment.
Retire keeps personal data; Wipe resets the device. Autopilot Reset keeps enrollment and Entra join.
Device query requires Advanced Analytics licensing (Intune Plan 2 / Suite or included in M365 E3 from July 2026).
commonPitfalls: Configuring the same setting in a settings catalog policy and a security baseline with different values; both report Conflict and the setting does not apply.
Using user groups with filters on device properties for shared devices and getting unexpected results when different users sign in.
Running 'Wipe' when 'Retire' was intended on a personal device, causing data loss and a very unhappy partner.
Expecting iOS restriction settings to apply to unsupervised (BYOD) devices.
fieldExperience: A filter per device model (e.g., all Teams Rooms or meeting PCs) is easier to maintain than separate groups, especially when the customer's IT contact adds devices themselves.
We create a saved KQL query library for helpdesk use (installed app version, service state, disk space) so first-line agents don't need a remote session for 'is X installed?'.
Always collect diagnostics before resetting a device that failed Autopilot; once reset, the evidence is gone.
revisionNotes: Settings catalog > templates for most settings; ADMX import for third-party apps; OMA-URI for gaps.
GPA: import XML > review MDM support > Migrate to settings catalog.
Filters: Include/Exclude, managed devices vs managed apps, evaluated at check-in.
Retire = company data only; Wipe = factory reset; Fresh Start = reinstall Windows; Autopilot Reset = keep enrollment.
Bulk actions: up to 100 devices; collect diagnostics for Windows from device blade or troubleshooting.

modules.title: Intune Suite and Plan 2 capabilities: EPM, Enterprise App Catalog, Remote Help, Cloud PKI, Tunnel for MAM, Advanced Analytics
learningObjectives: Configure Endpoint Privilege Management elevation settings and elevation rules
Deploy apps from the Enterprise App Catalog
Plan and configure Remote Help including RBAC permissions and unattended scenarios
Set up Microsoft Cloud PKI root and issuing CAs and SCEP profiles
Explain Microsoft Tunnel for MAM and Advanced Analytics capabilities and licensing
modules.executiveSummary:
Intune Plan 1 is the base product included in Microsoft 365 Business Premium, E3 and E5. **Intune Plan 2** and the **Intune Suite** add advanced capabilities: Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM), Enterprise App Management (Enterprise App Catalog), Remote Help, Microsoft Cloud PKI, Microsoft Tunnel for MAM and Advanced Analytics (device query, anomaly detection, enhanced Endpoint analytics). Microsoft's planning guide states that from July 2026 these capabilities are distributed across Microsoft 365 tiers: **E3 includes Plan 2, Remote Help and Advanced Analytics; E5/E7 add EPM, Cloud PKI and Enterprise App Management**; other plans (including Business Premium) buy Suite as an add-on.

For the exam, focus on what each capability solves and its key configuration objects rather than pricing.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Lets standard users run specific files elevated via rules (automatic, user confirmed, support approved, deny) using a virtual account.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Removes the need for local admin rights while still supporting legitimate elevation.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Microsoft-prepared Win32 app packages (with install commands and detection rules) that you add and update from Intune.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Removes packaging effort for common third-party apps and simplifies patching.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Cloud remote assistance with Entra authentication on both sides, Intune RBAC, compliance warnings and session auditing.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Secure alternative to Quick Assist/third-party tools that works within the tenant.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Cloud-hosted two-tier PKI (root + issuing CA, or BYOCA issuing CA) with a built-in SCEP registration authority.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Issues certificates for Wi-Fi/VPN authentication without NDES, the certificate connector or on-premises AD CS.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Extends Microsoft Tunnel VPN Gateway to unenrolled iOS/Android devices using app protection and app configuration policies.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Gives BYOD users secure access to on-premises apps without MDM enrollment.

modules.deepDive:
### Endpoint Privilege Management

- Two policy types under Endpoint security > Endpoint Privilege Management: **Windows elevation settings policy** (enables EPM, sets default elevation response: deny all, require support approval, require user confirmation; reporting scope) and **Windows elevation rules policy** (up to 100 rules per policy).
- A rule identifies a file by name plus file hash and/or certificate, optional file path (recommended in a location standard users cannot modify) and optional allowed arguments.
- Elevation types: **Automatic** (silent, requires file hash), **User confirmed** (optional business justification and/or Windows authentication), **Support approved** (admin approves request), **Elevate as current user**, **Deny** (deny wins over allow).
- Rules can be created from the **Elevation report** or a support approved request.

### Enterprise App Catalog

- Apps > All apps > Create > Enterprise App Catalog app; pick app and version; install/uninstall commands and detection rules are prefilled (editable). Supports supersedence for updates and is supported in Autopilot device preparation.

### Remote Help

- Enable at Tenant administration > Remote Help; optionally allow unenrolled devices.
- Licences required for both helper and sharer.
- RBAC permissions: View screen, Take full control, Elevation, Android/Windows unattended control, Remote tasks - Offer remote assistance, Remote Assistance Connector - Read. Built-in Help Desk Operator includes the attended permissions.
- Unattended Windows control: physical, corporate-owned, Entra joined/hybrid joined device with the Azure Virtual Desktop agent + bootloader and Remote Desktop enabled.
- Deploy the Windows app as Enterprise App Catalog or Win32 (remotehelpinstaller.exe /quiet acceptTerms=1).

### Microsoft Cloud PKI

1. Tenant administration > Cloud PKI > create **root CA** (validity, EKUs, key size/hash).
2. Create **issuing CA** anchored to the root (or BYOCA issuing CA signed by your own private CA).
3. Download public keys; create **trusted certificate profiles** for root and issuing CA per platform.
4. Create **SCEP certificate profiles** with the SCEP URI (keep {{CloudPKIFQDN}}), link the root trusted profile.
5. CRL and AIA endpoints are hosted by Intune; keys are HSM-backed (software-backed in trials).

### Microsoft Tunnel for MAM

- Requires an existing Microsoft Tunnel Gateway (Linux server/container).
- Android: app configuration policy for Microsoft Defender (tunnel client), app configuration for Edge (identity switch/strict tunnel), app protection policy that starts the tunnel. iOS: Tunnel for MAM iOS SDK in the apps.
- A device uses either MDM Tunnel or MAM Tunnel configurations, not both.

### Advanced Analytics

- Device query (single and multiple devices, KQL subset), anomaly detection, enhanced device timeline and battery health reports, resource performance.
modules.architecture: These capabilities plug into existing Intune building blocks: EPM uses an EPM client component installed on Windows when an elevation settings policy is assigned, and elevations run in a virtual account isolated from the user profile. Enterprise App Catalog apps are standard Win32 apps delivered by the IME. Remote Help uses Entra authentication for helper and sharer, Intune RBAC for authorisation and Azure-hosted relay endpoints (443). Cloud PKI consists of the Cloud PKI service (CAs with Azure Managed HSM keys), a cloud SCEP registration authority and validation service that checks the SCEP challenge is from an Intune-managed device. Tunnel for MAM keeps the Tunnel Gateway on-premises/in Azure but authorises connections per app identity rather than per device.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: removing local admin rights at the accountancy firm**

The tax software vendor ships quarterly updates that require elevation. With **EPM** we create a 'User confirmed' rule bound to the vendor's code-signing certificate and the install path, with business justification required. The vendor's support tool gets a 'Support approved' rule so our helpdesk approves each use. Default elevation response is 'Require support approval', so unknown installers create a ticket rather than silently failing.

**Remote Help** replaces the third-party remote tool: helpdesk staff see a compliance warning before connecting and every session is audited, which the firm's GDPR officer appreciated. **Cloud PKI** issues device certificates for the office Wi-Fi (WPA2/3-Enterprise via the firewall's RADIUS), eliminating the shared Wi-Fi password that had been on the reception whiteboard for years.

Licensing note for the proposal: the firm is on Business Premium, so these features are quoted as an Intune Suite add-on (or individual add-ons), a recurring line item in our managed service agreement.
examTips: EPM needs both an elevation settings policy (enables EPM) and an elevation rules policy; a deny rule overrides allow rules for the same file.
Automatic elevation rules require a file hash; certificates plus a protected file path are recommended for user confirmed rules.
Remote Help requires a licence for helper and sharer, and RBAC permissions; unattended control has strict device requirements.
Cloud PKI removes NDES and the certificate connector; you still need trusted certificate profiles and SCEP profiles per platform.
Tunnel for MAM is for unenrolled iOS/Android devices and needs an existing Microsoft Tunnel Gateway.
commonPitfalls: Creating EPM rules by file name only, allowing any renamed executable to elevate.
Assigning Remote Help permissions without scoping them, giving all helpdesk staff unattended control of every device.
Selecting 'Any Purpose' EKU or forgetting the root CA trusted profile, so Cloud PKI SCEP certificates fail to issue.
Mixing MDM Tunnel and MAM Tunnel configurations on the same enrolled device.
fieldExperience: Start EPM with the default response 'Require support approval' for a few weeks and build rules from the elevation report; you discover the real elevation needs of an SMB very quickly.
For customers without E5, compare Suite cost with what they pay for third-party remote control and PKI; the business case often closes on Remote Help plus Cloud PKI alone.
revisionNotes: Plan 1 = base (BP/E3/E5); Plan 2/Suite add Remote Help, EPM, EAM, Cloud PKI, Tunnel for MAM, Advanced Analytics.
EPM elevation types: automatic, user confirmed, support approved, elevate as current user, deny.
Remote Help RBAC: view screen, full control, elevation, unattended control, offer remote assistance.
Cloud PKI: root CA > issuing CA > trusted cert profiles > SCEP profile with SCEP URI.
Device query = Advanced Analytics; KQL subset; 1,000 multi-device queries per month limit.

learningObjectives: Create antivirus, firewall and attack surface reduction policies in the Endpoint security node
Configure silent BitLocker encryption, recovery key escrow, self-service recovery and the encryption report
Deploy security baselines and resolve conflicts with other policy types
Connect Intune to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, onboard devices with EDR policy and use risk score in compliance
Configure App Control for Business with the Intune Management Extension as managed installer
modules.executiveSummary:
The **Endpoint security** node in Intune groups focused policy types: Antivirus, Disk encryption, Firewall, Endpoint detection and response (EDR), Attack surface reduction, Account protection, App Control for Business, Endpoint Privilege Management, plus **Security baselines**. They all deliver CSP settings, just like configuration profiles, so conflicts are possible and must be avoided by design (use either baselines or endpoint security policies for the same setting).

The Defender for Endpoint integration is a key exam topic: a **service-to-service connection** (Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint) lets Intune retrieve the onboarding package automatically ('Auto from connector' in the EDR policy) and lets Defender's **device risk score** feed Intune compliance, which Conditional Access then enforces.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Purpose-built policy types (Antivirus, Firewall, ASR, EDR, Disk encryption, Account protection, App Control) in Intune's Endpoint security node.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Let security admins manage only security-relevant settings with dedicated RBAC (Endpoint Security Manager).

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Microsoft-recommended preconfigured groups of settings (Windows, Defender for Endpoint, Microsoft Edge, Windows 365, M365 Apps) that you can customise and version.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Fast route to a hardened, documented configuration.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Encryption without user prompts: Require Device Encryption = Enabled, Allow Warning For Other Disk Encryption = Disabled, Allow Standard User Encryption = Enabled, no TPM startup PIN.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Guarantees encryption on Entra joined devices without relying on the user; recovery keys escrow to Entra ID.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Endpoint detection and response profile that onboards devices to Defender for Endpoint using 'Auto from connector' or a pasted onboarding blob.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Each device must be onboarded with a tenant-specific package to send telemetry to Defender.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Policies via the ApplicationControl CSP (successor of AppLocker CSP) that allow only trusted code; the IME can be set as managed installer so Intune-deployed apps are trusted automatically.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Application allow-listing is one of the strongest controls against ransomware and unapproved software.

modules.deepDive:
### Antivirus and firewall

- **Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Antivirus** profile: real-time protection, cloud-delivered protection level, sample submission, PUA protection, scan schedule, exclusions, network protection (audit first).
- Related profiles: Defender update controls, Windows Security experience, tamper protection (requires MDE).
- **Firewall** profile for domain/private/public profiles and **Firewall rules** profile for per-app/port rules; rules from multiple policies merge.

### Attack surface reduction

- Profiles: **Attack Surface Reduction Rules**, **Device control**, App and browser isolation, Exploit protection, Application control (legacy AppLocker CSP).
- Modes per rule: Not configured, Off, Block, Audit, Warn. Start in Audit except for the standard protection rules (for example block credential stealing from LSASS), which can go straight to Block.
- ASR rules from different policies (endpoint security, endpoint protection template, MDE baseline) **merge** into a superset; only conflicting settings are held back.

### Disk encryption

- Endpoint security > Disk encryption > **BitLocker** profile (or Personal Data Encryption); macOS uses **FileVault**.
- Silent encryption prerequisites: TPM 1.2/2.0, WinRE enabled, UEFI for TPM 2.0, Entra joined (keys escrow to Entra ID automatically).
- Recovery keys: Devices > device > Recovery keys (audited), Entra admin center, or user **self-service** via the Company Portal / My Account. Reading keys requires microsoft.directory/bitlockerKeys/key/read (Cloud Device Administrator, Helpdesk Administrator, Global Administrator).
- **Rotate BitLocker keys** device action and 'Configure Recovery Password Rotation' (rotate after use).
- Monitor with **Devices > Monitor > Encryption report**.

### Security baselines

- Endpoint security > Security baselines; create a profile per baseline version, customise, assign.
- Avoid configuring the same setting in baselines and endpoint security/configuration policies; compliance policy values win over configuration policies, configuration conflicts must be resolved manually (per-setting status report).

### Defender for Endpoint integration

1. In the Defender portal enable the Microsoft Intune connection; in Intune turn on the MDE connector (Endpoint security > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint / Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens) and enable 'Connect Windows devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint' for compliance.
2. Create **EDR** policy: Platform Windows, profile Endpoint detection and response, package type **Auto from connector**, sample sharing. Or use 'Deploy preconfigured policy' on the EDR Onboarding Status tab.
3. Add 'Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score' to the Windows compliance policy; CA enforces.
4. Verify with a detection test and the EDR onboarding status report.

Roles: Endpoint Security Manager in Intune and Security Administrator in Entra ID for the connection. Onboarding to MDE also onboards the device to Endpoint DLP. Business Premium includes Defender for Business (built on MDE) rather than MDE Plan 2.

### App Control for Business

- Endpoint security > App Control for Business: built-in controls (trust Windows components, store apps, reputable apps via ISG, apps from managed installer) or custom XML; Audit or Enforce.
- Enable the **managed installer** policy for the Intune Management Extension so Win32/Store/Enterprise App Catalog apps deployed by Intune are tagged as trusted.
modules.architecture:
All endpoint security profiles compile to CSPs: Defender CSP, Firewall CSP, BitLocker CSP, ApplicationControl CSP, Policy CSP (ASR), LAPS CSP. Intune evaluates conflicts per setting across all policy types targeting a device.

Defender for Endpoint integration has two directions: **Intune > MDE** (onboarding blob via EDR policy; security settings management) and **MDE > Intune** (device risk level used in compliance evaluation, vulnerability data used by the Vulnerability Remediation Agent and Security tasks). Conditional Access consumes only the resulting compliance state, which is why the chain 'MDE risk > Intune compliance > Entra CA' is a classic exam pattern.

BitLocker recovery passwords are generated on the device and backed up to the Entra device object before encryption starts in silent mode; Entra ID stores up to 200 keys per device.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: ransomware-hardening sprint for the accountancy firm**

1. **Baseline vs policies**: we choose endpoint security policies (not the full Windows baseline) because the firm's tax software breaks on a few baseline settings; we document every deviation.
2. **Antivirus**: cloud protection high, PUA block, network protection in audit for two weeks then block; tamper protection on.
3. **ASR**: standard protection rules in Block, Office child process and macro rules in Audit for 14 days (the accountants use Excel macros heavily), then Warn, then Block with two exclusions.
4. **BitLocker**: silent encryption, XTS-AES 256, recovery password rotation after use; the encryption report goes into the monthly customer report.
5. **Defender**: the firm upgraded to Defender for Business via Business Premium; devices onboard through the EDR policy and risk score 'Medium' is added to compliance, so a compromised laptop is cut off from Microsoft 365 automatically.
6. **App Control** in audit with managed installer enabled; enforcement planned after we have three months of audit data.
examTips: Silent BitLocker: Require Device Encryption Enabled + Allow Warning For Other Disk Encryption Disabled (+ Allow Standard User Encryption for standard users); TPM startup PIN breaks silent mode.
Use 'Auto from connector' in EDR policy once the Intune-MDE connection is enabled; otherwise paste the onboarding blob from the Defender portal.
MDE risk score in a compliance policy + 'require compliant device' CA = block risky devices.
ASR rules from multiple sources merge; conflicting settings are held back, other settings apply.
App Control for Business uses the ApplicationControl CSP; the ASR 'Application control' profile uses the older AppLocker CSP.
Compliance policy settings override configuration settings; multiple compliance policies use the most restrictive value.
commonPitfalls: Deploying a security baseline and an endpoint security policy that set the same setting differently, then wondering why it shows Conflict.
Enabling silent BitLocker on devices that already run third-party encryption, leading to data loss.
Putting all ASR rules straight into Block mode for an Office-heavy customer and breaking macros on day one.
Forgetting that Entra ID stores a maximum of 200 BitLocker keys per device; when reached, silent encryption fails.
fieldExperience: For SMB customers we standardise on endpoint security policies plus a small number of settings catalog policies, and use security baselines only as a reference to compare against; it keeps conflict troubleshooting manageable.
Audit mode is only useful if someone looks at the data: we schedule a 30-minute review of ASR audit events in the Defender portal before switching to Block.
Self-service BitLocker recovery via My Account removes a surprising number of out-of-hours calls from travelling partners.
revisionNotes: Endpoint security node: Antivirus, Disk encryption, Firewall, EDR, ASR, Account protection, App Control, EPM, baselines.
MDE connector + EDR policy (Auto from connector) + risk score in compliance + CA.
BitLocker keys: Intune device > Recovery keys, Entra, self-service; rotation action; encryption report.
ASR modes: Off, Block, Audit, Warn; standard protection rules can go to Block directly.
App Control: managed installer = IME tags Intune-deployed apps as trusted.

modules.title: Device updates: update rings, feature and quality updates, Windows Autopatch, hotpatch, Apple and Android updates
learningObjectives: Design update rings with deferrals, deadlines and grace periods
Use feature update policies to pin or upgrade Windows versions and expedite quality updates
Implement Windows Autopatch groups and hotpatch
Manage iOS/iPadOS and macOS updates with DDM in the settings catalog and Android updates with policies or FOTA
Configure Delivery Optimization and monitor update compliance
modules.executiveSummary:
Intune manages Windows updates with several complementary policy types: **update rings** (client behaviour: deferrals, deadlines, restarts, user experience), **feature update policies** (lock or move devices to a specific Windows version), **quality update policies** (expedite and hotpatch), and **driver update policies**. **Windows Autopatch** orchestrates these through Autopatch groups and deployment rings, and since 2025 is available to Business Premium, A3+, E3+ and F3 licences. **Hotpatch** installs monthly security updates without a restart on eligible Windows 11 24H2+ devices.

Apple devices are updated with **declarative device management (DDM)** settings in the settings catalog (latest version enforcement or targeted version with a deadline); Android updates use system update policies in device restrictions or **FOTA** for Samsung/Zebra. **Delivery Optimization** reduces bandwidth for updates and Win32 apps.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A policy applying Windows Update client settings: quality deferral 0-30 days, feature deferral 0-365 days, deadlines 2-30 days, grace period 0-7 days, restart and UX settings.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Creates staged rollout (test, pilot, broad) and predictable restart behaviour.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Targets a specific Windows version (for example Windows 11 25H2); devices on older versions upgrade, newer ones are never downgraded.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Version control independent of ring deferrals; stays in force until changed.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: A quality update policy that pushes a specific security update immediately, overriding deferrals.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Respond quickly to actively exploited vulnerabilities.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Cloud service in Intune that automates Windows, Microsoft 365 Apps, Edge and Teams updates via Autopatch groups and deployment rings.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Reduces admin effort while keeping control (pause, rollback, phased releases).

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Monthly B-release security updates that take effect without a restart, with quarterly baseline cumulative updates that still need a restart.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Faster compliance and less user disruption.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Peer-to-peer and caching download technology for Windows updates, Store apps, Microsoft 365 Apps and Intune Win32 apps; download mode 0/1/2/3/99/100.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Saves WAN/internet bandwidth, especially in small offices with limited connectivity.

modules.deepDive:
### Update rings

| Setting | Range |
|---|---|
| Quality update deferral | 0-30 days |
| Feature update deferral | 0-365 days |
| Feature update uninstall period | 2-60 days |
| Deadline for feature updates | 2-30 days |
| Deadline for quality updates | 2-30 days |
| Grace period | 0-7 days |

- Pause (feature or quality) lasts up to 35 days; Uninstall can roll back the latest update.
- If you use feature update policies, set the ring's **feature update deferral to 0** and don't pause feature updates in the ring.
- 'Upgrade Windows 10 devices to Latest Windows 11 release' exists in rings; feature update policies give more control.
- Licensing: update rings need Intune Plan 1; feature update policies also need a Windows licence with the Autopatch entitlement (Business Premium, E3/E5, A3/A5, F3, VDA).
- Windows LTSC supports quality updates only.

### Feature updates

- Devices > Windows > Manage updates > Windows 10 and later updates > Feature updates > Create profile.
- Only one feature update is offered at a time - the latest applicable across policies; Windows 11 beats Windows 10.
- Safeguard holds block devices with known issues.
- Require telemetry at least 'Required' and the Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant service running.
- Rollout options: make available ASAP, on a date, or gradually.

### Windows Autopatch and hotpatch

- Tenant administration > Windows Autopatch > **Autopatch groups**: deployment rings (Test, Ring1, ... Last) with assigned or dynamically distributed device groups; Autopatch creates update ring and feature update policies per ring.
- Don't assign your own update rings to Autopatch-managed devices.
- **Hotpatch** prerequisites: Windows 11 24H2+, eligible licence (Windows Enterprise E3/E5, M365 F3, Education A3/A5, Business Premium, Windows 365 Enterprise), latest baseline, **VBS enabled**, Intune quality update policy with hotpatch on. Arm64 needs CHPE disabled.

### Apple and Android

- iOS/iPadOS 17+ and macOS 14+: settings catalog > Declarative Device Management > **Software Update** (Target OS Version, Target Date Time, Details URL) or **Software Update Enforce Latest** (Delay in Days, Install Time). DDM settings take precedence over Restrictions-based deferral. MDM-based update policies are deprecated.
- Restrictions: Defer software updates and delay visibility 0-90 days (supervised).
- Android Enterprise: device restrictions > system update (automatic, postponed, maintenance window); **FOTA** for Samsung (Knox E-FOTA) and Zebra LifeGuard OTA for firmware-level control.

### Delivery Optimization

- Configuration profile > Templates > Delivery Optimization or settings catalog. Download modes: 0 HTTP only, 1 LAN (same NAT), 2 Group, 3 Internet, 99 Simple, 100 Bypass.
- Microsoft Connected Cache can complement DO for larger sites.

### Monitoring

- Reports > Windows updates (feature update report, expedited quality update report), Windows Autopatch reports (quality/feature update status, device alerts, hotpatch quality update report). Requires Windows diagnostic data to be enabled for the tenant.
modules.architecture:
Update rings write Update CSP values on the device; Windows Update on the device decides when to download/install within those constraints. Feature update, quality (expedite/hotpatch) and driver policies are **cloud-side** controls in the Windows Autopatch deployment service: Intune registers the device and Windows Update only offers the content that is approved for that device. That's why feature update policies need diagnostic data and Entra joined/hybrid joined devices, and why they don't apply during OOBE.

On Apple devices, DDM moves the update lifecycle to the device: it receives a declaration with the target version and deadline, downloads, notifies and enforces locally, and reports status back asynchronously.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: patch management as a managed service**

For the accountancy firm we run **Windows Autopatch** with three rings: Test (our MSP's own demo device and the office manager's laptop, 0-day deferral), Ring1 (5 volunteers, 2 days), Last (everyone else, 7 days, 3-day deadline, 2-day grace). Tax season (March-June) has a **feature update freeze**: the feature update policy pins Windows 11 24H2 until July, then moves to the next version.

All laptops are Windows 11 24H2 with VBS, so **hotpatch** is on: partners stopped complaining about reboot prompts during client meetings. When a critical zero-day lands, we **expedite** the quality update to all rings within hours.

iPhones get a DDM 'Enforce Latest' policy with 7 days delay and install time 22:00. Delivery Optimization mode 1 (LAN) is set because the office has a modest fibre connection and 35 laptops downloading 4 GB feature updates at 09:00 would kill Teams calls.
examTips: Ranges to memorise: quality deferral 0-30, feature deferral 0-365, deadlines 2-30, grace 0-7, uninstall window 2-60 days, pause 35 days.
When combining feature update policies with rings, set ring feature deferral to 0 and don't pause features in the ring.
Feature update policies never downgrade and don't apply during Autopilot OOBE.
Hotpatch needs Windows 11 24H2+, VBS, eligible licence, current baseline and a quality update policy with hotpatch enabled.
Apple updates: use DDM settings catalog (Software Update / Enforce Latest); MDM-based Apple update policies are deprecated.
Expedite overrides deferrals for a specific quality update; it is the answer for 'deploy this security update now'.
commonPitfalls: Assigning both an Autopatch-managed ring and a custom update ring to the same device, causing conflicting deferrals.
Leaving a 30-day feature deferral in rings and wondering why the feature update policy doesn't upgrade devices.
Disabling the Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant service (wlidsvc) through hardening; feature updates are then never offered.
Deploying a Windows 11 feature update to Windows 10 devices that aren't capable, which then stop getting Windows 10 feature updates.
fieldExperience: A 'Test' ring containing the MSP's own lab device per customer catches most breaking changes before the customer sees them.
Customers understand deadlines and grace periods better when we translate them into 'you will be forced to restart at most X days after release'.
For Apple devices, include a Details URL pointing to a short Dutch/French help page; it reduces 'what is this update popup' tickets.
revisionNotes: Rings = client behaviour; feature/quality/driver policies = cloud deployment service controls.
Feature update licence: Intune Plan 1 + Windows licence with Autopatch entitlement.
Autopatch: Autopatch groups, deployment rings, creates ring + feature policies; available to BP, A3+, E3+, F3.
Hotpatch: rebootless monthly security, quarterly baseline restart, VBS required.
DO download modes: 0, 1 LAN, 2 Group, 3 Internet, 99 Simple, 100 Bypass.
