modules.executiveSummary:
Intune supports many app types; the exam expects you to pick the right one and know its delivery mechanics. **Win32 apps** (.intunewin created by IntuneWinAppUtil.exe) are the most flexible on Windows: detection rules, requirements, dependencies, supersedence, delivery optimization, restart behaviour and ESP tracking, installed by the **Intune Management Extension**. **Microsoft Store apps** use WinGet; **Enterprise App Catalog** apps are Microsoft-prepackaged Win32 apps. **Microsoft 365 Apps** can be deployed with the built-in app type (Office CSP, configuration designer or XML) or as a Win32 package when it must be tracked during the ESP.

On mobile, store apps are distributed via **Apple Business Manager apps and books (VPP)** and **Managed Google Play**; LOB apps (.ipa/.apk) are possible too. Assignments are Required, Available for enrolled devices, Available with or without enrollment, or Uninstall.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool; -c setup folder, -s setup file, -o output folder, -q quiet. Produces a .intunewin.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Compresses and encrypts installer content and extracts metadata so Intune can deliver Win32 apps.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: MSI product code, file/folder, registry or custom script logic that tells the IME whether the app is installed.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Determines success/failure and drives reinstall, supersedence and ESP tracking.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Supersedence replaces/updates an older app version; dependencies install prerequisite Win32 apps first (automatically if configured).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Controlled app lifecycle without manual uninstall/reinstall.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Built-in Intune app using the Office CSP; configure apps, architecture, update channel, version, languages, shared computer activation, or XML from ODT.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Simple suite deployment from the Office CDN with no packaging.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Policies that mute notifications from Microsoft apps (for example Outlook, Teams) on iOS/Android outside working hours.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Supports employee well-being and right-to-disconnect requirements.

modules.deepDive:
### Win32 app lifecycle

1. Test silent install/uninstall manually; note install folder or product code for detection.
2. Package: IntuneWinAppUtil -c C:\src\App -s setup.exe -o C:\out -q (keep the tool outside the source folder). Max app size 30 GB.
3. Intune admin center > Apps > All apps > Create > Windows app (Win32): upload .intunewin.
4. **Program**: install/uninstall command, install behaviour (System or User), restart behaviour, return codes. A PowerShell script installer can replace the command line.
5. **Requirements**: architecture, minimum OS, disk/RAM, custom requirement script.
6. **Detection rules**: MSI, file, registry or script.
7. **Dependencies** and **Supersedence** (update or uninstall previous version).
8. **Assignments**: Required / Available / Uninstall, with filters, delivery optimization priority, notifications, availability and installation deadline.

The IME downloads content (via Delivery Optimization), decrypts, runs the installer in the chosen context, evaluates detection and reports. Logs: C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs (IntuneManagementExtension.log, AppWorkload.log).

### Choosing the Windows app type

| Need | App type |
|---|---|
| EXE/complex installer, detection, dependencies | Win32 |
| Common third-party app without packaging | Enterprise App Catalog (Plan 2/Suite) |
| Store app with WinGet | Microsoft Store app (new) |
| Single MSI, simple | LOB MSI (avoid mixing with Win32 during ESP) |
| Office suite | Microsoft 365 Apps app type (or Win32 for ESP-tracked install) |
| Web shortcut | Web link |

### Microsoft 365 Apps

- Configuration designer: apps, other licensed apps (Project/Visio), 32/64-bit, update channel (Current, Monthly Enterprise, Semi-Annual Enterprise), remove other (MSI) versions, version to install, shared computer activation, accept EULA, languages.
- Or Enter XML data (ODT configuration.xml).
- Policies for Microsoft 365 Apps: settings catalog (Office ADMX) or **Cloud Policy** in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center (config.office.com), which also provides inventory, servicing profiles and security update status.
- During Autopilot ESP, deploy M365 Apps as Win32 (ODT setup.exe + XML) to avoid install concurrency issues.

### Mobile apps

- **iOS**: store apps via ABM Apps and Books (VPP) location token; device licensing allows install without Apple ID; LOB .ipa; web clips.
- **Android**: Managed Google Play (approve apps, private apps, web apps); required apps on corporate devices; personally owned work profile installs into the work profile.
- Assignment 'Available with or without enrollment' targets MAM users.

### Monitoring and troubleshooting

- App > Device install status / User install status; Troubleshooting + support blade for a user; Reports > Apps (app install status, discovered apps).
- Common errors: 0x87D1041C (detection rule not found after install), install context mismatch, missing dependency, 'Not applicable' due to requirements.
modules.architecture:
Windows LOB MSI, Store and Microsoft 365 Apps app types are delivered through MDM CSPs (EnterpriseDesktopAppManagement, Office CSP). Win32, PowerShell scripts, Remediations, Enterprise App Catalog and new Store apps are handled by the **Intune Management Extension** agent, which Intune installs automatically when the first such workload is assigned. The IME polls for assignments (roughly every hour and at sign-in), downloads encrypted content from Intune's CDN with Delivery Optimization, and reports results back.

On iOS the MDM channel installs App Store/VPP apps (licence assigned to device or user) and can make apps 'managed' (required for app configuration via MDM and for removal on retire). On Android Enterprise, Managed Google Play is the app source; Intune approves apps in the Google tenant and Android Device Policy installs them.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: standard app set for the accountancy firm**

| App | Type | Assignment |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft 365 Apps (Monthly Enterprise, 64-bit, NL/FR/EN) | Win32 (ODT) | Required, devices, ESP-blocking |
| Accounting software (vendor EXE + MSI prerequisites) | Win32 with dependency | Required, ESP-blocking |
| eID middleware for Belgian ID cards | Win32 | Required |
| 7-Zip, Adobe Reader, Notepad++ | Enterprise App Catalog / Store | Available in Company Portal |
| Teams/Outlook on iPhone | VPP device licences | Required |

The accounting app's detection rule checks the version of the main executable; when the vendor releases an update we create a new Win32 app with **supersedence** (update) and assign it to the pilot group first. A **Quiet Time** policy mutes Outlook and Teams notifications on phones between 19:00 and 07:00 and at weekends, which the firm included in its right-to-disconnect policy (relevant under Belgian labour law for employers with 20+ employees).
examTips: IntuneWinAppUtil switches: -c source folder, -s setup file, -o output folder, -q quiet.
Win32 apps are installed by the Intune Management Extension; it supports Entra joined, Entra registered, hybrid joined and GPO-enrolled devices.
Don't mix LOB MSI and Win32 apps during the ESP; deploy Microsoft 365 Apps as Win32 if it must be tracked by the ESP.
Supersedence can update or replace an app; dependencies can auto-install prerequisites.
'Available for enrolled devices' requires enrollment; 'Available with or without enrollment' is for MAM scenarios.
Microsoft 365 Apps policies can come from Intune settings catalog or Cloud Policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
commonPitfalls: Packaging the content prep tool inside the source folder, bloating the .intunewin.
Detection rule that checks a file the installer doesn't create, so Intune reports failure and reinstalls endlessly.
Installing a user-context app as required to a device group without a signed-in user.
Forgetting 'Remove other versions' when upgrading from MSI Office, causing the M365 Apps install to fail.
fieldExperience: Keep a per-customer package repository with source, install/uninstall commands, detection logic and the .intunewin in the documentation platform; repackaging under pressure is where mistakes happen.
For SMBs with Plan 2/Suite, the Enterprise App Catalog removes most packaging work for common tools; we only hand-package the line-of-business software.
Always test installs in SYSTEM context with PsExec -s before uploading; many vendor installers behave differently as SYSTEM.
revisionNotes: Win32: .intunewin, install context, requirements, detection, dependencies, supersedence, max 30 GB.
IME logs in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs.
M365 Apps: configuration designer or XML; Cloud Policy at config.office.com.
iOS store apps via ABM Apps and Books (VPP); Android via Managed Google Play.
Assignment intents: Required, Available (enrolled), Available with or without enrollment, Uninstall.

learningObjectives: Design app protection policies for iOS/iPadOS, Android and Windows (Edge) for managed and unmanaged devices
Target policies by device management state using filters
Enforce app protection with Conditional Access grant controls
Create app configuration policies through the managed devices and managed apps channels
Apply the data protection framework (levels 1-3)
modules.executiveSummary:
**App protection policies (APP / MAM)** protect organisation data inside apps that integrate the Intune App SDK (Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, Edge, Office and many partner apps), with or without device enrollment. They control data movement (save as, cut/copy/paste, open-in, backups), access requirements (PIN, biometrics, sign-in) and conditional launch (jailbreak/root, minimum OS/app version, offline grace, threat level). Selective wipe removes only organisation data.

They become enforceable when combined with **Conditional Access** grant **Require app protection policy** (often 'or' **Require approved client app**) on iOS/Android. **App configuration policies** push settings to apps, either through the MDM OS channel (managed devices) or the Intune App SDK channel (managed apps), for example 'only allow work or school accounts' in Outlook.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: User-targeted rules for data protection, access requirements and conditional launch applied to MAM-enabled apps in a work context.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Protects company data on BYOD without managing the whole device.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Using managed-app filters (unmanaged vs managed device) so BYOD gets stricter rules than enrolled devices.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Avoids double friction on corporate devices while hardening personal ones.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Conditional Access grant control that only allows client apps with an Intune APP applied; needs a broker app (Authenticator on iOS, Company Portal on Android).
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Prevents users from bypassing MAM with native mail apps or unprotected clients.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Key/value (or settings catalog for Edge on Windows) configuration delivered to apps via managed devices or managed apps channel.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Preconfigures apps (accounts, allowed domains, features) and supports scenarios like Tunnel for MAM.

coreConcepts.whatItIs: Microsoft's tiered APP recommendations: Level 1 enterprise basic, Level 2 enhanced, Level 3 high data protection.
coreConcepts.whyItExists: Gives a defensible baseline instead of inventing settings per customer.

modules.deepDive:
### Creating an app protection policy

Intune admin center > Apps > Protection > Create policy > iOS/iPadOS or Android (Windows for Edge MAM):

1. **Apps**: target core Microsoft apps, all Microsoft apps, or specific/custom apps; choose app types (all, unmanaged, managed) or use filters.
2. **Data protection**: backup org data (block iCloud/Android backup), send org data to other apps (policy managed apps), save copies of org data (block, allow OneDrive/SharePoint), restrict cut/copy/paste, encrypt org data, screen capture, printing.
3. **Access requirements**: PIN for access, biometrics instead of PIN, PIN reset after N days, work account credentials, recheck after N minutes.
4. **Conditional launch**: max PIN attempts, offline grace period (block/wipe), jailbroken/rooted devices (block/wipe), minimum OS/app/SDK version, device manufacturer, Play Integrity verdict, max allowed device threat level (MTD/Defender).
5. **Assignments**: user groups (APP is user-targeted), with exclusions.

Windows MAM protects Microsoft Edge on unmanaged Windows devices, with Conditional Access 'Require app protection policy' for Windows (and Windows Security Center health via the MTD connector).

### Conditional Access for MAM

- Policy: All users (exclude break-glass), All resources, Condition: Device platforms Android + iOS, Grant: **Require approved client app** OR **Require app protection policy** (Require one of the selected controls). Start in report-only.
- Device must register in Entra ID via a broker: Microsoft Authenticator (iOS) or Company Portal (Android) - users don't need to enroll.
- Requires Microsoft Entra ID P1.

### App configuration

- **Managed devices**: Apps > Configuration > Create > Managed devices; iOS (configuration designer or XML, app must be managed/deployed by Intune) or Android Enterprise (permissions, JSON or designer, app from Managed Google Play).
- **Managed apps**: SDK channel, works without enrollment (for example Edge homepage, allowed accounts). On Windows only Microsoft Edge is supported for managed apps configuration.
- Example: Outlook 'Allowed account mode' to block personal accounts on managed devices.

### BYOD restrictions

- MAM without enrollment can't deploy apps, certificates, Wi-Fi or VPN profiles; the user installs apps from the store.
- Use platform enrollment restrictions to block personal device enrollment when you want MAM-only BYOD.
modules.architecture:
The Intune App SDK inside the app checks in with the Intune MAM service using the user's identity (not the device's) after sign-in. Policies apply only when the app operates in the work context (identity-based multi-identity). On unenrolled iOS devices Microsoft Authenticator acts as the broker for device registration and token issuance; on Android the Company Portal hosts the MAM agent and broker. Conditional Access reads the app's MAM compliance via the token issuance flow (the app must request the token through the broker).

App configuration via managed devices travels on the OS MDM channel (Apple Managed App Configuration, Android managed configurations); via managed apps it travels on the MAM channel and requires the SDK. Selective wipe is a MAM command executed by the SDK the next time the app launches.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: partners using personal phones**

Three partners refuse to enroll their personal Android and iPhone devices. We implement:

- An **APP for unmanaged devices** (filter: managed apps, device management type = unmanaged) at data protection framework Level 2: no copy/paste to personal apps, save only to OneDrive/SharePoint, PIN or biometrics, block on rooted/jailbroken devices, wipe after 30 days offline.
- A lighter **APP for managed devices** (company iPhones) because the device is already supervised and passcode-protected.
- **Conditional Access**: iOS/Android require approved client app OR app protection policy; native mail apps no longer work, Outlook does.
- **App configuration (managed apps)** for Outlook and Edge with the firm's domain as allowed account.

When a partner left the firm, a **selective wipe** removed mailbox data and OneDrive files from his personal phone while his holiday photos stayed untouched, exactly as promised in the BYOD policy signed at onboarding.
examTips: APP is assigned to user groups and works with or without enrollment; selective wipe removes only org data.
CA for MAM: device platforms iOS/Android + grant 'Require approved client app' or 'Require app protection policy' with 'require one of the selected controls'.
Broker apps: Microsoft Authenticator for iOS, Company Portal for Android; needed for app-based CA even without enrollment.
Use filters (managed apps) on device management type to have different APP for unmanaged vs managed devices.
App configuration: 'Managed devices' channel needs the app delivered by Intune MDM; 'Managed apps' channel needs the Intune App SDK.
Windows MAM protects Microsoft Edge only (managed apps configuration on Windows supports Edge only).
commonPitfalls: Blocking 'Save copies of org data' without allowing OneDrive for Business/SharePoint, so users can't save attachments anywhere.
Assigning APP to device groups (they are user-targeted) and seeing no effect.
Creating the CA policy without the broker app on devices, generating confused users stuck in an install loop.
Expecting MAM-only BYOD devices to receive Wi-Fi or certificate profiles.
fieldExperience: Present the BYOD option to SMB management as 'we protect the company data, not the phone'; acceptance rises sharply compared to full enrollment.
Pilot APP with a small group first; overly strict clipboard rules are the most common source of complaints (copying a client number from Teams to a banking app).
revisionNotes: APP sections: data protection, access requirements, conditional launch, assignments (users).
Data protection framework levels 1/2/3.
App-based CA needs Entra ID P1 and a broker app.
App config: managed devices (MDM channel) vs managed apps (SDK channel).
MAM without enrollment can't push apps, certificates, Wi-Fi or VPN.

modules.executiveSummary:
The smallest domain (10-15%) but highly practical. Everything in Intune is exposed through **Microsoft Graph** (deviceManagement and deviceAppManagement namespaces); the **Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK** (Connect-MgGraph with scopes such as DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All) is the standard automation tool, and app-only authentication with certificates is used for unattended runbooks. **Custom compliance** uses a PowerShell discovery script plus JSON rules.

The 2026 objectives add **Security Copilot agents in Intune** (Change Review, Device Offboarding, Policy Configuration and Vulnerability Remediation agents) that analyse data and propose actions for admin approval. Monitoring covers **Intune reports** (operational, organisational, historical, exportable), **Endpoint analytics** (startup performance, application reliability, work from anywhere, baselines and insights) and **Remediations** (detection + remediation script packages, scheduled or run on demand), plus tenant health via service health and message center.

modules.deepDive:
### Graph and PowerShell

- Install-Module Microsoft.Graph; Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All"; Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice -Filter "complianceState eq 'noncompliant'".
- Beta cmdlets (Microsoft.Graph.Beta.*) expose newer Intune features; v1.0 is preferred when available.
- Device actions via Graph (sync, wipe, retire, clean Windows device) and bulk exports (reports export jobs).
- Unattended automation: Entra app registration with application permissions + certificate, run in Azure Automation or another scheduler; least privilege scopes.
- Graph API for Intune requires an active Intune licence in the tenant.

### Custom compliance

1. Devices > Compliance > Scripts > Add (Windows): PowerShell script returning a compressed JSON of key/values.
2. Windows compliance policy > Custom Compliance > select script + upload JSON rules.
3. Evaluated by the IME; results appear in compliance reports.

### Security Copilot agents

- **Vulnerability Remediation Agent**: uses Defender Vulnerability Management data (needs MDE P2 or DVM standalone) to list prioritised CVEs with step-by-step Intune remediation; mark suggestions as applied.
- **Change Review Agent**: evaluates Multi Admin Approval requests and recommends approve/reject.
- **Device Offboarding Agent**: finds stale or misaligned devices across Intune and Entra; admin approval before offboarding.
- **Policy Configuration Agent**: turns documents/plain language into settings catalog recommendations.
- Prerequisites: Intune Plan 1, Security Copilot with SCUs, plugins (Intune, Defender), RBAC; agents use an agentic identity with delegated permissions verified by a readiness check.

### Reporting and alerts

- Reports node: Device compliance, Device configuration, Windows updates, Endpoint security (Defender antivirus, firewall, encryption), Endpoint analytics; operational reports for daily work, organisational for summaries; most can be exported (CSV) and accessed via Graph export jobs.
- Diagnostic settings can send Intune audit and operational logs to Log Analytics for **workbooks** and alerting.
- Service health and message center in the Microsoft 365 admin center (and Tenant administration > Tenant status in Intune) for incidents and change notices.
- Alerts: Intune alert rules (for example Cloud PKI, Autopatch device alerts) and Azure Monitor alerts on Log Analytics data for compliance drift, enrollment failures and configuration conflicts.

### Endpoint analytics

- Enable data collection (Intune data collection policy for all cloud-managed devices). Data appears up to 24 hours after a restart; at least 5 devices needed for a score.
- **Startup performance**: core boot and sign-in times, restart frequency, impactful processes, GP impact.
- **Application reliability**: app reliability score, mean time to failure, crashes.
- **Work from anywhere**: cloud management, cloud identity, cloud provisioning, Windows 11 readiness.
- Advanced Analytics adds anomaly detection, device timeline, battery health and device query.

### Remediations

- Devices > Manage devices > Scripts and remediations > Create script package: upload detection and remediation .ps1 (UTF-8), run as system or user, 32/64-bit, enforce signature check, assign with schedule (once, hourly, daily).
- Up to 200 script packages; output limit 2,048 characters; detection exit 1 = issue detected.
- **Run remediation** device action for on-demand fixes.
- Licensing: Windows Enterprise E3/E5, Education A3/A5 or Windows VDA per user; devices Entra joined or hybrid joined and enrolled or co-managed.
modules.architecture: Graph sits in front of every Intune service; the admin center itself is a Graph client, which is why anything visible in the portal is scriptable. Endpoint analytics collects functional data from devices (Windows diagnostic data / Intune data collection) into the Microsoft cloud, computes scores per device, model and app, and benchmarks them. Remediations and custom compliance scripts are executed by the IME, which reports output back to Intune. Security Copilot agents run in the Security Copilot platform, read Intune/Defender data through plugins with an agentic identity and write suggestions back to the Intune Agents node; changes still require an administrator.
modules.realWorldExample:
**Scenario: monthly MSP service report and proactive fixes**

Our MSP runs an Azure Automation runbook per customer (app-only Graph, certificate auth, read-only scopes) that exports noncompliant devices, devices not synced for 30 days and BitLocker status into the monthly report PDF for the accountancy firm.

Endpoint analytics showed **startup performance** 20 points below baseline; the culprit was a legacy PDF printer service starting at boot. A **Remediation** (detection: service start type Automatic; remediation: set to Manual) fixed it on all devices in a day. A second remediation clears the Teams cache when the Teams app reliability score drops.

The customer has E3 licences for two partners only; because Remediations need Windows Enterprise E3/E5 per user, we discussed upgrading the rest of the firm as part of the next licence renewal, rather than running Remediations unlicensed.
examTips: Remediation script runs only if the detection script exits with code 1; scripts must be UTF-8, scheduled via assignment, max 200 packages.
Remediations require Windows Enterprise E3/E5 (or A3/A5, VDA) per user - Business Premium alone does not list it.
Endpoint analytics score = Startup performance + Application reliability + Work from anywhere; needs at least 5 devices.
Custom compliance = PowerShell discovery script + JSON rules file in a Windows compliance policy.
Security Copilot agents need Security Copilot capacity (SCUs); the Vulnerability Remediation Agent also needs Defender Vulnerability Management data.
Use Connect-MgGraph with least-privileged scopes; beta cmdlets for preview features.
commonPitfalls: Saving remediation scripts as UTF-8 with BOM while enforcing signature check, causing failures.
Putting reboot commands or secrets in remediation scripts.
Granting DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All to a reporting script that only needs read access.
Judging Endpoint analytics a day after enabling it, before devices have restarted and reported.
fieldExperience: Build remediations as 'detect only' first; the detection report alone often reveals how widespread an issue is before you change anything.
Multi-tenant MSP automation works best with one app registration per customer tenant, certificate auth and read-only scopes for reporting; write access only for specific runbooks.
Endpoint analytics baselines are great sales material for laptop refresh projects: show the customer how much time slow devices cost them per month.

flashcards.front: Three ways a device gets an identity in Microsoft Entra ID?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Entra registered (BYOD), Microsoft Entra joined (corporate cloud-native) and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined (corporate + on-prem AD).

flashcards.front: Which setting makes Entra joined Windows devices auto-enroll into Intune?
flashcards.back: MDM user scope (All or Some) under Windows Automatic Enrollment; requires Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2.

flashcards.front: Dynamic rule for all Autopilot devices?
flashcards.back: (device.devicePhysicalIDs -any (_ -startsWith "[ZTDid]")). Group tag = [OrderID]:<tag>.

flashcards.front: What connects Intune to Apple Business Manager for ADE?
flashcards.back: An enrollment program token (.p7m) created with the Intune public key; renewed yearly. APNs certificate is a separate prerequisite.

flashcards.front: Android Enterprise mode for a userless single-app kiosk?
flashcards.back: Corporate-owned dedicated device (COSU).

flashcards.front: Default of 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as'?
flashcards.back: Compliant. Change it to Not compliant when you use Conditional Access.

flashcards.front: Default compliance status validity period?
flashcards.back: 30 days (configurable 1-120). Devices that don't report in time become noncompliant.

flashcards.front: Role assignment components in Intune RBAC?
flashcards.back: Role (permissions) + Members (admin groups) + Scope (groups) + Scope tags (visibility). Permissions are additive; no deny.

flashcards.front: Where do you create a Windows LAPS policy in Intune?
flashcards.back: Endpoint security > Account protection > Windows > Local admin password solution (Windows LAPS). Assign to device groups.

flashcards.front: What must be enabled in Entra before Intune LAPS can back up to Entra ID?
flashcards.back: Devices > Device settings > Enable Microsoft Entra Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS).

flashcards.front: Which Autopilot mode works on Hyper-V VMs?
flashcards.back: User-driven. Self-deploying and pre-provisioning need physical TPM 2.0 attestation.

flashcards.front: Autopilot device name template rules?
flashcards.back: Max 15 characters, letters/numbers/hyphens, not all numbers; macros %SERIAL% and %RAND:x%.

flashcards.front: How do you start pre-provisioning at OOBE?
flashcards.back: Press the Windows key five times and choose pre-provision (technician flow), then reseal.

flashcards.front: Error 0x800705B4 during self-deploying mode?
flashcards.back: Timeout - typically no TPM 2.0 attestation support (e.g., a VM).

flashcards.front: Key differences of Autopilot device preparation?
flashcards.back: No hardware hash needed, enrollment time grouping into a static device group, up to 25 apps and 10 scripts during OOBE, granular reporting.

flashcards.front: What does the ESP setting 'Block device use until all apps and profiles are installed' do?
flashcards.back: Keeps the user on the ESP until required apps/profiles finish (or selected blocking apps), preventing desktop access.

flashcards.front: Windows 365 network option required for hybrid join?
flashcards.back: Azure network connection (ANC). Microsoft-hosted network is recommended for Entra join.

flashcards.front: Tool to analyse GPOs for MDM support and migrate them?
flashcards.back: Group Policy analytics > Migrate to a settings catalog policy.

flashcards.front: Retire vs Wipe?
flashcards.back: Retire removes company data/apps/management, keeps personal data. Wipe factory-resets the device.

flashcards.front: EPM elevation types?
flashcards.back: Automatic, User confirmed (justification/Windows auth), Support approved, Elevate as current user, Deny (deny wins).

flashcards.front: What does Microsoft Cloud PKI replace?
flashcards.back: On-prem CA, NDES and the Intune Certificate Connector; provides root/issuing CA and a cloud SCEP registration authority.

flashcards.front: Licence needed for device query (KQL)?
flashcards.back: Advanced Analytics (Intune Plan 2/Suite; included in Microsoft 365 E3 from July 2026 per the Intune planning guide).

flashcards.front: Silent BitLocker key settings?
flashcards.back: Require Device Encryption = Enabled; Allow Warning For Other Disk Encryption = Disabled; Allow Standard User Encryption = Enabled; no TPM startup PIN.

flashcards.front: Where do admins view BitLocker recovery keys in Intune?
flashcards.back: Devices > select device > Recovery keys (access is audited). Encryption report: Devices > Monitor > Encryption report.

flashcards.front: EDR package type when the MDE connector is active?
flashcards.back: Auto from connector. Otherwise paste the onboarding blob ('Onboard').

flashcards.front: How does a risky device lose access to Microsoft 365?
flashcards.back: MDE risk score in Intune compliance policy > device noncompliant > Conditional Access 'require compliant device' blocks.

flashcards.front: How do ASR rules from multiple policies combine?
flashcards.back: They merge into a superset; only conflicting settings are held back.

flashcards.front: Update ring deferral ranges?
flashcards.back: Quality 0-30 days, feature 0-365 days; deadlines 2-30 days; grace period 0-7 days.

flashcards.front: Feature update policy + update ring: what ring setting?
flashcards.back: Feature update deferral = 0 and don't pause feature updates in the ring.

flashcards.front: Hotpatch prerequisites?
flashcards.back: Windows 11 24H2+, eligible licence (E3/E5, F3, A3/A5, Business Premium, W365 Enterprise), latest baseline, VBS on, quality update policy with hotpatch.

flashcards.front: How to manage iOS 17+/macOS 14+ updates in Intune?
flashcards.back: Settings catalog > Declarative Device Management > Software Update or Software Update Enforce Latest.

flashcards.front: IntuneWinAppUtil parameters?
flashcards.back: -c setup folder, -s setup file, -o output folder, -q quiet, -h help.

flashcards.front: Which agent installs Win32 apps?
flashcards.back: The Intune Management Extension (IME). Logs in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs.

flashcards.front: Win32 detection rule types?
flashcards.back: MSI product code, File/folder, Registry, Custom script.

flashcards.front: Why deploy Microsoft 365 Apps as Win32 during ESP?
flashcards.back: The built-in M365 Apps type isn't managed by the IME and can install concurrently with Win32 apps, causing ESP failures.

flashcards.front: App protection policies are assigned to...?
flashcards.back: User groups. They work with or without device enrollment.

flashcards.front: CA grant controls for MAM on iOS/Android?
flashcards.back: Require approved client app OR Require app protection policy (require one of the selected controls).

flashcards.front: Broker apps for app-based Conditional Access?
flashcards.back: Microsoft Authenticator on iOS; Company Portal on Android.

flashcards.front: App configuration channels?
flashcards.back: Managed devices (OS MDM channel, app deployed by Intune) and Managed apps (Intune App SDK, works without enrollment).

flashcards.front: When does a Remediation's remediation script run?
flashcards.back: Only when the detection script exits with code 1.

flashcards.front: Remediations licensing?
flashcards.back: Windows Enterprise E3/E5 (incl. M365 F3/E3/E5), Education A3/A5 or Windows VDA per user.

flashcards.front: Endpoint analytics score components?
flashcards.back: Startup performance, Application reliability, Work from anywhere (weighted average).

flashcards.front: Custom compliance building blocks?
flashcards.back: PowerShell discovery script + JSON rules file in a Windows compliance policy.

flashcards.front: Four Security Copilot agents in Intune?
flashcards.back: Change Review, Device Offboarding, Policy Configuration, Vulnerability Remediation.

flashcards.front: Graph PowerShell: list noncompliant devices?
flashcards.back: Connect-MgGraph -Scopes DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All; Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice -Filter "complianceState eq 'noncompliant'".

labs.title: Windows Autopilot user-driven Microsoft Entra join with a Hyper-V VM
labs.technology: Windows Autopilot, Intune, Microsoft Entra ID
labs.objective: Register a Hyper-V virtual machine in Windows Autopilot, target it with a dynamic group, ESP and user-driven deployment profile, and complete a zero-touch Microsoft Entra join and Intune enrollment.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 trial or developer tenant (recommended: Microsoft 365 E5 or Business Premium trial, which include Intune Plan 1 and Microsoft Entra ID P1). Never use a customer production tenant for labs.
A test user licensed for Intune and Microsoft Entra ID P1 (included in the trial licences).
Admin account with Intune Administrator (or Policy and Profile Manager + Entra Groups Administrator).
Hyper-V host (Windows 11 Pro/Enterprise) with a Windows 11 Enterprise or Pro ISO; VM with at least 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, generation 2, Secure Boot and virtual TPM enabled.
Internet access for the VM (Autopilot, Entra ID, Intune and Windows Update endpoints).

steps.title: Allow Entra join and configure automatic enrollment
steps.instructions:
1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center (entra.microsoft.com) go to **Entra ID > Devices > Device settings** and make sure **Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra** is set to All or to a group containing your test user.
2. In the Intune admin center (intune.microsoft.com) go to **Devices > Enrollment > Windows** tab > **Automatic Enrollment**.
3. Set **MDM user scope** to **Some** and select a group that contains your test user (or All in a lab). Leave the MDM URLs at their defaults and **Save**.

steps.title: Create the Hyper-V virtual machine
steps.instructions:
1. In Hyper-V Manager create a **Generation 2** VM named LAB-AP01 with 4096 MB startup memory (disable dynamic memory), 2 virtual processors and a 64 GB disk.
2. In VM **Settings > Security**, enable **Secure Boot** and **Trusted Platform Module**.
3. Attach the Windows 11 ISO, install Windows, and stop at the first OOBE screen (region selection). Create a **checkpoint** named 'OOBE-clean' so you can repeat the lab.

steps.title: Capture and upload the hardware hash
steps.instructions:
1. At the OOBE screen press **Shift+F10** to open a command prompt and start **powershell**.
2. Run:

    Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force
    Install-Script -Name Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo -Force
    Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo -OutputFile C:\HWID\LAB-AP01.csv

3. Copy the CSV to your admin PC (for example via a shared folder or by mounting the VHDX after shutdown), or use **Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo -Online -GroupTag LAB-AP** to upload directly (requires consent for the Graph app).
4. If using the CSV: Intune admin center > **Devices > Enrollment > Windows > Windows Autopilot > Devices > Import**, select the CSV and wait until the import completes. Open the device and set **Group tag** to **LAB-AP**.

steps.title: Create a dynamic device group
steps.instructions:
1. Intune admin center > **Groups > New group**: Security group, name **LAB-DEV-Autopilot**, membership type **Dynamic Device**.
2. **Add dynamic query** > Edit rule syntax:

    (device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[OrderID]:LAB-AP"))

3. Save and create. Membership evaluation can take several minutes; check the group's **Members** blade until LAB-AP01 (shown by serial number) appears.

steps.title: Create and assign an Enrollment Status Page profile
steps.instructions:
1. **Devices > Enrollment > Windows > Enrollment Status Page > Create**.
2. Name **LAB-ESP**; Show app and profile configuration progress = **Yes**; installation timeout 60 minutes; Show custom message on error = Yes; **Allow users to collect logs** = Yes; **Block device use until all apps and profiles are installed** = **Yes**; Allow users to reset device if installation error occurs = Yes; Allow users to use device if installation error occurs = No.
3. Assign to **LAB-DEV-Autopilot**. If you already have a Win32 app (see the Win32 lab), add it under blocking apps with **Selected**.

steps.title: Create and assign the Autopilot deployment profile
steps.instructions:
1. **Devices > Enrollment > Windows > Windows Autopilot > Deployment Profiles > Create profile > Windows PC**.
2. Name **LAB-AP-UserDriven**; Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot = No.
3. OOBE: Deployment mode **User-driven**; Join to Microsoft Entra ID as **Microsoft Entra joined**; Microsoft Software License Terms **Hide**; Privacy settings **Hide**; Hide change account options **Hide**; User account type **Standard**; Allow pre-provisioned deployment **No**; Language **Operating system default**; Automatically configure keyboard **Yes**; Apply device name template **Yes** with **LAB-%RAND:5%**.
4. Assign to **LAB-DEV-Autopilot** and create.
5. Back in **Windows Autopilot > Devices**, select **Sync** and wait until the device shows **Profile status: Assigned**.

steps.title: Optionally assign the device to the test user
steps.instructions: In **Windows Autopilot > Devices**, select the device > **Assign user**, choose the test user and set a friendly name. The sign-in page will then be pre-populated with the user's UPN.

steps.title: Run the deployment
steps.instructions:
1. Restore the 'OOBE-clean' checkpoint (or restart the VM if it never left OOBE). The device must reach the internet before the region screen to download its Autopilot profile; if it was already at OOBE when the profile was assigned, restart it.
2. Choose region and keyboard if prompted; you should see the company branding and the sign-in page.
3. Sign in as the test user and complete MFA.
4. Watch the ESP phases: **Device preparation**, **Device setup**, **Account setup**.
5. Set up Windows Hello for Business if prompted.

steps.title: Verify the result in Intune and Entra
steps.instructions:
1. Intune admin center > **Devices > Windows** - the device appears with the name LAB-xxxxx, ownership **Corporate**, primary user = test user.
2. Open the device > **Enrollment** to see the Autopilot profile and ESP results.
3. Entra admin center > **Devices > All devices** - join type **Microsoft Entra joined**, MDM **Microsoft Intune**.
4. On the VM run **dsregcmd /status** and confirm AzureAdJoined : YES.

validation: The Autopilot device shows Profile status 'Assigned' before deployment.
The VM displays the tenant's sign-in page during OOBE and doesn't show EULA or privacy screens.
After deployment the device is Microsoft Entra joined, enrolled in Intune as corporate, and named according to the template.
The signed-in user is a standard user (net localgroup administrators doesn't list the user).
Devices > Monitor > Autopilot deployments (or the device's Enrollment blade) shows a successful deployment.
troubleshooting: No Autopilot experience at OOBE: profile not yet assigned or the VM reached OOBE before assignment - check Profile status, then restart the VM.
Device not in the dynamic group: verify the group tag spelling and rule syntax ([OrderID]:LAB-AP), and allow time for evaluation.
Enrollment error 'MDM terms of use' or 80180018: user isn't in the MDM user scope or lacks an Intune licence.
ESP timeout: check blocking apps; on the device press Shift+F10 and run mdmdiagnosticstool.exe -area Autopilot -cab C:\temp\ap.cab, or use the 'collect logs' button.
Self-deploying or pre-provisioning tests fail on this VM with 0x800705B4: expected, those modes need physical TPM 2.0.
cleanup: Delete the device from Devices > All devices (Intune) and from Entra ID > Devices.
Delete the Autopilot registration (Windows Autopilot > Devices > Delete) so the hash can be reused.
Remove the deployment profile, ESP profile and LAB-DEV-Autopilot group assignments, then delete them.
Delete the Hyper-V VM and its checkpoints.

labs.title: Compliance policy plus Conditional Access requiring a compliant device
labs.objective: Create a Windows compliance policy with actions for noncompliance, harden tenant compliance settings and enforce device compliance with a Conditional Access policy, rolled out in report-only first.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 trial or developer tenant (recommended: Microsoft 365 E5 or Business Premium trial, which include Intune Plan 1 and Microsoft Entra ID P1). Never use a customer production tenant for labs.
Roles: Intune Administrator (or Policy and Profile Manager) and Conditional Access Administrator.
One Intune-enrolled Windows 11 device (for example the VM from the Autopilot lab) and one unenrolled browser/device for negative testing.
A break-glass (emergency access) account that is excluded from all Conditional Access policies.
Test user with Exchange Online / SharePoint licence.

steps.title: Harden tenant-wide compliance settings
steps.instructions:
Intune admin center > **Endpoint security > Device compliance > Compliance policy settings** (also reachable via Devices > Compliance):
- **Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as** = **Not compliant**
- **Compliance status validity period (days)** = 30 (default)

Save.

steps.title: Create a notification message template
steps.instructions: **Devices > Compliance > Notifications > Create notification**: name LAB-Noncompliant, add a subject and body (for example in Dutch and English) explaining how to fix compliance via Company Portal. Save.

steps.title: Create a Windows compliance policy
steps.instructions:
**Devices > Compliance > Create policy > Windows 10 and later**:
- Device Health: **Require BitLocker** = Require, **Require Secure Boot** = Require
- Device Properties: **Minimum OS version** = a current Windows 11 build (for example 10.0.26100)
- System Security: **Firewall** = Require, **Microsoft Defender Antimalware** = Require, **Real-time protection** = Require
- (Optional, if MDE connected) **Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score** = Medium

steps.title: Configure actions for noncompliance and assign
steps.instructions: On **Actions for noncompliance**: keep **Mark device noncompliant** with schedule **1 day** (grace period), add **Send email to end user** using LAB-Noncompliant, immediately. Assign the policy to the test **user** group (or device group). Create.

steps.title: Check compliance on the test device
steps.instructions: On the Windows device open **Company Portal > Devices > Check status** (or Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Info > Sync). In Intune open **Devices > Windows > [device] > Device compliance** and review per-setting status. Fix any noncompliant setting (for example enable BitLocker) until the device is **Compliant**.

steps.title: Create the Conditional Access policy in report-only
steps.instructions:
Entra admin center > **Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy**:
- Name: LAB-CA-RequireCompliantDevice
- Users: Include your test user group; **Exclude** the break-glass account
- Target resources: Include **Office 365** (or All resources in a lab)
- Conditions > Device platforms: Include **Windows** (optional for the lab)
- Grant: **Grant access** > **Require device to be marked as compliant**
- Enable policy: **Report-only** > Create

steps.title: Analyse report-only results
steps.instructions: Sign in as the test user from the compliant device and from an unenrolled browser/device. In Entra > **Sign-in logs**, open each sign-in > **Report-only** tab and confirm the expected result: Success (compliant device) vs Failure (unmanaged).

steps.title: Enforce the policy
steps.instructions: Edit the policy and switch **Enable policy** to **On**. Repeat both sign-ins: the compliant device gets access; the unenrolled device is blocked with a message that the device must be managed/compliant.

validation: The test device shows Compliant in Intune and in Entra (device 'Compliant' column = Yes).
Sign-in from the compliant device succeeds with the CA policy On.
Sign-in from an unmanaged browser/device is blocked by LAB-CA-RequireCompliantDevice (visible in sign-in logs).
Turning off BitLocker or the firewall on the device makes it 'In grace period' then 'Not compliant' after one day, and access is blocked.
troubleshooting: Compliant in Intune but blocked: the device may be registered twice or the browser doesn't pass the device identity (use Edge signed in with the work profile or the Windows account extension in Chrome).
Device stays 'Not evaluated': check that a policy is assigned to the user/device and trigger a sync.
Everyone locked out: sign in with the break-glass account and set the policy to Off; always keep that exclusion.
BitLocker check fails on a VM: the setting relies on Device Health Attestation; use a VM with vTPM and Secure Boot or test with OS version instead.
cleanup: Set the CA policy to Off and delete it.
Delete the compliance policy and notification template.
Restore 'Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as' if the lab tenant is shared with other labs.

labs.title: Windows LAPS with Intune and Microsoft Entra ID
labs.technology: Intune endpoint security (account protection), Microsoft Entra ID
labs.objective: Enable Windows LAPS in Microsoft Entra ID, deploy an Intune LAPS policy that backs up the built-in administrator password to Entra ID, retrieve the password and rotate it manually.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 trial or developer tenant (recommended: Microsoft 365 E5 or Business Premium trial, which include Intune Plan 1 and Microsoft Entra ID P1). Never use a customer production tenant for labs.

Roles: Intune Administrator or Endpoint Security Manager (to create the policy) plus a Microsoft Entra role allowed to read device local administrator passwords (for example Cloud Device Administrator).
One Microsoft Entra joined, Intune-enrolled Windows 11 device (current build with Windows LAPS built in).

steps.title: Enable LAPS in Microsoft Entra ID
steps.instructions: Entra admin center > **Entra ID > Devices > All devices > Device settings** > set **Enable Microsoft Entra Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS)** to **Yes** > Save.

steps.title: Create a device group
steps.instructions: Create a security group **LAB-DEV-LAPS** (assigned) and add the test device. LAPS policies should target device groups, not user groups.

steps.title: Enable the managed account (optional but common)
steps.instructions: The built-in Administrator account is disabled by default. Either create a settings catalog policy (**Devices > Configuration > Create > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog > Local Policies Security Options > Accounts Enable Administrator Account Status = Enable**) assigned to LAB-DEV-LAPS, or plan to manage a dedicated local account that you create separately. LAPS manages an existing account; it doesn't create one.

steps.title: Create the LAPS policy
steps.instructions:
Intune admin center > **Endpoint security > Account protection > Create Policy** > Platform **Windows**, Profile **Local admin password solution (Windows LAPS)** > Create.
- Name: LAB-LAPS
- **Backup Directory**: Backup the password to Microsoft Entra ID only
- **Password Age Days**: 30
- **Administrator Account Name**: leave blank (built-in admin via RID) or the name of your custom account
- **Password Complexity**: Large letters + small letters + numbers + special characters
- **Password Length**: 16
- **Post Authentication Actions**: Reset the password and logoff the managed account; **Post Authentication Reset Delay**: 8 hours

Assign to **LAB-DEV-LAPS** and create.

steps.title: Sync the device and confirm policy status
steps.instructions: Trigger a sync (Intune device blade > **Sync**). Open the LAB-LAPS policy and check **Device and user check-in status** shows Succeeded. On the device, Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > **LAPS > Operational** shows a successful password update/backup event.

steps.title: Retrieve the password
steps.instructions: Intune admin center > **Devices > All devices > [device] > Local admin password** > Show local administrator password. Alternatively Entra > Devices > [device] > Local administrator password recovery. Note the account name and last rotation time.

steps.title: Rotate the password manually
steps.instructions: On the device blade select **... > Rotate local admin password** and confirm. Device actions status shows **Pending**, then **Complete** after the device checks in. Retrieve the password again and confirm it changed.

steps.title: Review audit and reports
steps.instructions: Check Intune **Tenant administration > Audit logs** and Entra audit logs for the password read and the rotation action. Review the LAPS policy report for conflicts.

validation: LAB-LAPS policy shows Succeeded for the device.
A password and last rotation date are visible on the device's Local admin password blade.
Signing in locally (.\Administrator) with the retrieved password works.
After 'Rotate local admin password' the old password no longer works and a new one is shown.
Audit logs record each password read and manual rotation.
troubleshooting: No password shown: LAPS not enabled in Entra device settings, backup directory set to AD, or the device hasn't processed the policy yet.
Policy Conflict: another LAPS policy (or a settings catalog LAPS policy) targets the same device; keep one LAPS policy per device.
Manual rotation fails: the device never backed up a password or your role lacks Remote tasks: Rotate Local Admin Password.
Account not managed: Administrator Account Name doesn't match an existing account on the device.
cleanup: Delete the LAB-LAPS policy and the settings catalog policy that enabled the Administrator account.
Optionally disable LAPS in Entra device settings if the tenant is shared.

labs.title: Update rings, feature update policy and Delivery Optimization
labs.technology: Intune Windows update management, Windows Autopatch service
labs.objective: Design a two-ring Windows update strategy with deadlines, pin devices to a Windows 11 version with a feature update policy, configure Delivery Optimization and review the update reports.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 trial or developer tenant (recommended: Microsoft 365 E5 or Business Premium trial, which include Intune Plan 1 and Microsoft Entra ID P1). Never use a customer production tenant for labs. The Windows licence must include the Autopatch entitlement (Business Premium, E3/E5) for feature update policies.
Role: Policy and Profile Manager or Intune Administrator.
At least one Entra joined, Intune-enrolled Windows 11 Pro/Enterprise device.
Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Windows data: enable use of Windows diagnostic data (required for update reports), and devices with telemetry at least 'Required'.

steps.title: Create device groups for the rings
steps.instructions: Create two device security groups: **LAB-UPD-Pilot** (your test device) and **LAB-UPD-Broad** (empty or other devices).

steps.title: Create the Pilot update ring
steps.instructions:
Intune admin center > **Devices > Windows > Manage updates > Windows 10 and later updates > Update rings > Create profile**:
- Name: LAB-Ring-Pilot
- Microsoft product updates: Allow; Windows drivers: Allow
- **Quality update deferral period**: 0
- **Feature update deferral period**: 0 (feature versions will be controlled by a feature update policy)
- Feature update uninstall period: 14
- User experience: Automatic update behaviour = Reset to default; Option to pause = Disable
- **Use deadline settings**: Allow; Deadline for feature updates 2; Deadline for quality updates 2; Grace period 1; Auto reboot before deadline: Yes

Assign to LAB-UPD-Pilot.

steps.title: Create the Broad update ring
steps.instructions: Copy the settings with **Quality update deferral period** = 7, feature deferral 0, deadlines 3 (quality) and 7 (feature), grace period 2. Name LAB-Ring-Broad, assign to LAB-UPD-Broad. Make sure no device is in both groups.

steps.title: Create a feature update policy
steps.instructions:
**Windows 10 and later updates > Feature updates > Create profile**:
- Name: LAB-FU-Win11
- Feature update to deploy: a current Windows 11 version (for example Windows 11, version 24H2 or 25H2)
- Rollout options: Make update available as soon as possible (or gradual rollout in production)
- Accept the Windows 11 licence notice

Assign to both ring groups.

steps.title: Optional: expedite a quality update
steps.instructions: **Quality updates > Create profile**: select the latest security update and set **Number of days to wait before restart is enforced** to 1. Assign to LAB-UPD-Pilot only. Use this pattern for zero-day responses.

steps.title: Configure Delivery Optimization
steps.instructions:
**Devices > Configuration > Create > Windows 10 and later > Templates > Delivery Optimization**:
- Download mode: **HTTP blended with peering behind same NAT (1)**
- Delay background HTTP download: 60 seconds; Delay foreground HTTP download: 60 seconds
- Bandwidth: Percent with business hours (for example 20% during 08:00-18:00)

Assign to both ring groups.

steps.title: Sync and verify on the device
steps.instructions: Sync the device. On the device: **Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Configured update policies** lists the policies. Run Get-DeliveryOptimizationStatus in PowerShell after updates download to see peer statistics.

steps.title: Review reports
steps.instructions: Intune admin center > **Reports > Windows updates**: open **Feature updates** and **Windows Feature Update Report** for LAB-FU-Win11, and the update ring per-device status (Update rings > LAB-Ring-Pilot > Device status). Data can take up to 24 hours to appear.

validation: Each ring shows the device with Succeeded status and no conflicts.
The device lists the deferral/deadline policies under Configured update policies.
The feature update report shows the device as offered/installing/updated to the targeted version (or already on it).
No device is a member of both rings.
troubleshooting: Feature update not offered: check ring feature deferral is 0 and not paused, telemetry is at least Required, wlidsvc (Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant) is running, and no safeguard hold applies.
Report empty: Windows diagnostic data not enabled for the tenant or data not yet processed (allow 24 hours).
Device downgraded? It can't: feature update policies never downgrade; a newer version stays.
Ring conflict: the device is in two ring groups or also managed by Windows Autopatch.
cleanup: Delete the expedite policy, feature update policy, update rings and Delivery Optimization profile.

labs.title: App protection policies for iOS/Android BYOD with app-based Conditional Access
labs.technology: Intune app protection (MAM), Microsoft Entra Conditional Access
labs.objective: Protect company data in Outlook, Teams and OneDrive on unenrolled personal phones, enforce the use of protected apps with Conditional Access and perform a selective wipe.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 trial or developer tenant (recommended: Microsoft 365 E5 or Business Premium trial, which include Intune Plan 1 and Microsoft Entra ID P1). Never use a customer production tenant for labs.
Roles: Intune Administrator (or Application Manager) and Conditional Access Administrator.
A personal (unenrolled) iPhone or Android test phone with Outlook, Teams and OneDrive from the public store, plus Microsoft Authenticator (iOS) or Company Portal (Android) as broker.
Test user with Exchange Online and OneDrive licences and an exclusion-ready break-glass account.

steps.title: Create a managed apps filter for unmanaged devices
steps.instructions: Intune admin center > **Tenant administration > Filters > Create > Managed apps**: name LAB-Unmanaged-Apps, platform iOS/iPadOS (create a second filter for Android), rule **(app.deviceManagementType -eq "Unmanaged")**.

steps.title: Create the iOS app protection policy
steps.instructions:
**Apps > Protection > Create policy > iOS/iPadOS**:
- Apps: **Core Microsoft Apps** (includes Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, Edge, Office)
- Data protection: Backup org data to iTunes and iCloud = **Block**; Send org data to other apps = **Policy managed apps**; Save copies of org data = **Block** with allowed storage **OneDrive for Business** and **SharePoint**; Restrict cut, copy and paste = **Policy managed apps with paste in**; Encrypt org data = Require
- Access requirements: PIN for access = Require; Simple PIN = Block; Touch ID/Face ID instead of PIN = Allow; Recheck access requirements after 30 minutes
- Conditional launch: Jailbroken/rooted devices = Block access; Offline grace period 720 minutes Block access, 90 days Wipe data; Min OS version = a supported iOS version
- Assign to the test user group with filter **Include LAB-Unmanaged-Apps**

steps.title: Create the Android app protection policy
steps.instructions: Repeat for **Android** with equivalent settings (Backup = Block, Screen capture = Block, Play Integrity verdict = basic integrity) and the Android unmanaged filter.

steps.title: Create an app configuration policy (managed apps) for Edge
steps.instructions: **Apps > Configuration > Create > Managed apps**: Select public apps > **Microsoft Edge** (iOS and Android). In **General configuration settings** add the key **com.microsoft.intune.mam.managedbrowser.homepage** with your intranet or SharePoint home URL. Assign to the test user group. This shows the MAM (SDK) configuration channel, which works without enrollment.

steps.title: Create the app-based Conditional Access policy
steps.instructions:
Entra admin center > **Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy**:
- Users: test user group; exclude break-glass
- Target resources: **Office 365**
- Conditions > Device platforms: **iOS** and **Android**
- Grant: **Require approved client app** and **Require app protection policy**, **Require one of the selected controls**
- Enable: Report-only first, then On

steps.title: Test on the phone
steps.instructions:
1. Sign in to Outlook with the test user. When prompted, install/open the broker app (Authenticator on iOS, Company Portal on Android) - no enrollment is needed.
2. Outlook informs you that your organisation now protects data; set the app PIN.
3. Try to copy text from an email into a personal notes app (blocked), save an attachment to Files/Downloads (blocked) and to OneDrive (allowed).
4. Try to add the account to the native Mail app (blocked by Conditional Access once the policy is On).

steps.title: Monitor
steps.instructions: Intune admin center > **Apps > Monitor > App protection status** and **Reports > App protection** to see the user, app and policy check-in.

steps.title: Perform a selective wipe
steps.instructions: **Apps > App selective wipe > Create wipe request**: choose the user and the device. Open Outlook on the phone; company data is removed while personal apps and data stay untouched. Check the wipe request status becomes **Completed**.

validation: App protection status report shows the user's apps checked in with LAB policies.
Copy/paste to unmanaged apps and saving to local storage are blocked; saving to OneDrive works.
Native mail app access is blocked by the CA policy (sign-in log shows the policy result).
Selective wipe completes and removes only company data.
troubleshooting: Policy not applied: the app wasn't signed in with the targeted user, the filter excludes the device, or the app isn't MAM-enabled.
Endless broker prompt: install Microsoft Authenticator (iOS) or Company Portal (Android) and sign in through the app again.
Corporate (enrolled) phones also get the strict policy: verify the filter uses deviceManagementType and create a separate policy for managed devices.
App protection changes can take time; force-close and reopen the app to trigger a check-in.
cleanup: Set the CA policy to Off and delete it.
Delete the app protection, app configuration policies and filters.
Remove the work account from the phone apps.

labs.title: Package and deploy a Win32 app with IntuneWinAppUtil
labs.technology: Intune Win32 app management, Intune Management Extension
labs.objective: Package a silent-installing application as .intunewin, configure install commands, requirements and a detection rule, deploy it as required and troubleshoot with the IME logs.
requirements: A Microsoft 365 trial or developer tenant (recommended: Microsoft 365 E5 or Business Premium trial, which include Intune Plan 1 and Microsoft Entra ID P1). Never use a customer production tenant for labs.
Role: Application Manager or Intune Administrator.
An admin workstation with the Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool (IntuneWinAppUtil.exe) downloaded from GitHub.
A sample MSI or EXE installer that supports silent installation (for example 7-Zip MSI x64).
An Intune-enrolled Windows 11 test device (for example from the Autopilot lab).

steps.title: Test the installer silently
steps.instructions:
On a test machine run the install and uninstall commands in an elevated prompt, for example:

    msiexec /i 7z-x64.msi /qn /norestart
    msiexec /x {PRODUCT-CODE} /qn

Note the install folder (C:\Program Files\7-Zip) and the MSI product code for detection.

steps.title: Prepare source and output folders
steps.instructions: Create C:\Packages\7zip\Source (installer only) and C:\Packages\7zip\Output. Keep IntuneWinAppUtil.exe outside the Source folder, otherwise it gets packaged too.

steps.title: Create the .intunewin package
steps.instructions:
Run:

    IntuneWinAppUtil.exe -c C:\Packages\7zip\Source -s 7z-x64.msi -o C:\Packages\7zip\Output -q

The tool creates 7z-x64.intunewin and, for MSI files, extracts metadata such as the product code.

steps.title: Add the Win32 app in Intune
steps.instructions: Intune admin center > **Apps > All apps > Create** > App type **Windows app (Win32)** > Select. Upload the .intunewin; fill name, description and publisher (required); optionally category and logo; tick **Show this as a featured app** if desired.

steps.title: Configure program settings
steps.instructions:
- Install command: msiexec /i "7z-x64.msi" /qn /norestart (prefilled for MSI)
- Uninstall command: prefilled msiexec /x {product code} /qn
- Install behaviour: **System**
- Device restart behaviour: **App install may force a device restart** or **No specific action**
- Return codes: keep defaults (0 success, 1707 success, 3010 soft reboot, 1641 hard reboot, 1618 retry)

steps.title: Configure requirements and detection
steps.instructions:
- Requirements: Operating system architecture **x64**, Minimum operating system **Windows 10 22H2** or later
- Detection rules: **Manually configure** > Add > Rule type **MSI** (product code prefilled) - or **File**: path C:\Program Files\7-Zip, file 7z.exe, detection method File or folder exists

steps.title: Assign the app
steps.instructions: Skip dependencies and supersedence. On **Assignments** add your test device group under **Required**; end user notifications **Show all toast notifications**; Delivery optimization priority **Content download in background**. Review + create. Upload of the content must finish before devices can install it.

steps.title: Monitor installation and read logs
steps.instructions:
1. Sync the device (Company Portal > Settings > Sync or the Intune Sync action).
2. In Intune open the app > **Device install status**.
3. On the device review C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs\IntuneManagementExtension.log and AppWorkload.log for download, install and detection results.
4. Restart the 'Microsoft Intune Management Extension' service to force a new evaluation if needed.

steps.title: Add a supersedence update (optional)
steps.instructions: Package a newer version as a new Win32 app, and on its **Supersedence** page add the old app with **Uninstall previous version = No** (update in place). Assign to the same group and confirm the version is updated.

validation: Device install status shows Installed for the test device.
The app appears in Settings > Apps and in Company Portal as installed.
IME logs show 'Detected app' after install with exit code 0.
Uninstalling manually triggers reinstall at the next IME evaluation (required intent).
troubleshooting: 0x87D1041C: app installed but detection rule didn't find it - fix the path/product code or 32/64-bit registry redirection setting.
App 'Not applicable': requirements (architecture, OS version, disk space) not met.
Install stuck in 'Downloading': check Delivery Optimization and proxy access to Intune content endpoints.
User-context installer fails as System: change install behaviour or use a wrapper script.
cleanup: Change the assignment to Uninstall, wait for removal, then delete the app(s).
Delete the local packaging folders if no longer needed.
